why: DECIDABLE in form, with a stated undecidable residue. The claim is "the progeny of CD56bright are CD56dim" — a precursor-product statement, which the rubric puts on the decidable side. More importantly, its principal rival (Phase A's alternative: a pre-existing CD56dim population is selected/expanded, not converted; and the two-independent-pathway model) is a PURE CLONAL-STRUCTURE statement, and clonal structure is exactly what the primitive returns. "Do the CD56dim cells recovered descend from the CD56bright cells put in, or from a contaminating dim cell?" is answerable with shared-ancestor information and nothing else — it is the one question the barcoding primitive is definitionally competent to settle. Likewise "are CD56bright and CD56dim the same or different lineage" is the rubric's explicit DECIDABLE case, and it has already been posed and answered this way in a primate (Wu 2018, Sci Immunol, PMID 30389798: barcoded macaque HSPC transplant, CD56+CD16- vs CD56-CD16+ NK repertoires "remained distinct under homeostatic conditions over several years"). The load-bearing part of the primitive here is HOW RECENTLY, not merely WHETHER. Every NK cell in one person shares an HSPC ancestor, so bare ancestor-sharing is trivially TRUE under all models. The discriminating readout is whether a bright cell and a dim cell share a recent, post-NK-commitment ancestor (consistent with bright->dim) or only a distant progenitor-level one (two pools branching upstream, the Ding 2024 ENKP/ILCP architecture). UNDECIDABLE RESIDUE, stated explicitly. Surface NCAM1 density is an activation-modulable variable, so part of this claim is a reversible-state claim, and for that part both answers are consistent with the same clonal structure: a clone spanning both compartments is produced equally by (a) irreversible bright->dim maturation, (b) dim->bright, and (c) cells oscillating between two states. Lineage cannot order a reversible state. It also cannot separate "dim descend from bright" from "bright and dim are clonal siblings branching a few divisions upstream" at the resolution obtainable in a polyclonal human steady state — mtDNA marks label clades, not division events, and PMID 40134031 (Genome Biol 2025) shows mtDNA variants have "limited discriminatory power among different genuine lineages under weak clonal expansion," which is precisely the healthy-adult NK regime. So: the NEGATIVE is decisive (clonally discordant repertoires falsify the arrow), the POSITIVE is confounded on both direction and sibling-vs-parent. Decidable, but one-sidedly.
action_if_yes: IF YES (bright and dim share recent, post-commitment clones; bright-marked clones later appear in dim): Stated concretely, the next experiment would be to move from "there is a route" to "how fast and driven by what": longitudinal clone-level sampling in the same individual to fit a conversion rate, then a perturbation arm asking which signal drives it (the unreplicated Chan 2007 fibroblast/FGFR1 contact route vs the IL-2/IL-15/IL-12 route that Romagnani 2007 and Chan 2007 disagree about), and a translational arm barcoding a CD56bright-phenotype iPSC/CD34-derived NK product to confirm it matures in the recipient. Why this branch is weak, written out because B2 turns on it: (1) It is the default expectation, not a discovery. Shared clonal marks between two mature NK subsets are predicted by essentially every model on the table, including the competing one in which both subsets are fed independently from the same upstream progenitor clones. A YES therefore does not separate the claim from its main rival. (2) The direction it appears to license is not actually licensed. Establishing bright-before-dim requires ordering within a clone, which reversibility of CD56 density confounds and which mtDNA/integration-site resolution in a polyclonal steady state does not deliver. (3) The follow-ons are not contingent on the answer. Human in-vivo pulse-chase (the 6,6-D2-glucose sorted-subset design of Patel 2017, PMID 28606987 / PMC5502436, which has never been run on bright vs dim — the only NK deuterium study, PMID 17346281, sorted CD3-CD16+ only and did not resolve the subsets) is the assay that would actually settle direction, and it is a NON-lineage assay one would run instead of, not because of, the clonal experiment. The FGF-vs-cytokine mechanism question and the iPSC-NK maturation question are already being pursued by the field on the assumption that the answer is YES; a YES changes nobody's protocol. Net: YES confirms the textbook arrow, is non-discriminating against the sibling model, and redirects no downstream work.
action_if_no: IF NO (repertoires clonally discordant; bright-dominant clones stay bright over months-to-years and never seed dim): This branch is genuinely rich and the next experiments are specific and forced: (1) It replicates Wu 2018 (PMID 30389798) in the species that matters and kills the stage-4 -> stage-5 arrow of the Freud/Caligiuri five-stage human model, which is the one concrete named dependency Phase A left standing. The immediate follow-on is to look for the human counterpart of the two-pathway ontogeny reported in mouse (Ding 2024, Nat Immunol, PMID 38872000, ENKP vs ILCP): prospectively isolate the candidate human progenitors from bone marrow/tonsil and ask, clonally, which one feeds CD56dim. (2) It removes the mechanistic explanation for the GATA2-deficiency phenotype (Mace 2013, PMID 23365458: patients maintaining a CD56dim pool with essentially no CD56bright) and makes those patients the natural human genetic test bed rather than an anomaly. (3) It breaks a manufacturing rationale, which is the sharpest practical consequence. Current iPSC- and CD34-derived NK products come out CD56bright-phenotype and are infused on the assumption that they mature into cytotoxic CD56dim in the patient. Under NO, that assumption is void and the next experiment is defined: determine whether a CD56dim-committed product can be derived directly, and re-read existing infusion trials for whether the transferred bright product ever became dim. (4) It reclassifies CD56 density as a state/activation variable rather than a developmental stage, which changes how every NK scRNA-seq trajectory paper that orients its pseudotime by this arrow should be read.
compartments_needed: Two, and only two, for the core adjudication, both from peripheral blood of the same individual at the same draw: (A) CD3- CD56bright CD16- NK cells (B) CD3- CD56dim CD16+ NK cells Optional compartments that strengthen but are not required: (C) Bone marrow (aspirate) — to place the branch point relative to progenitors. (D) Secondary lymphoid tissue where CD56bright is enriched — tonsil (routine tonsillectomy waste) or lymph node (only at surgery). (E) The clonal-mark substrate, which is the real constraint rather than the tissue: NK cells have no rearranged antigen receptor, so there is no endogenous clone label of the kind the T/B fields get free. The mark must come from (i) somatic mtDNA or nuclear SNVs, (ii) lentiviral integration sites in HSC gene-therapy recipients, (iii) donor/recipient marks after allo-HSCT, or (iv) engineered barcodes, which in a primate means macaque.
compartments_obtainable: YES — and this is the strongest feature of D3. Compartments A and B are obtainable paired from one human, from one routine venipuncture, in any healthy adult, with no procedural gate whatsoever. Not post-mortem. Not surgery-only. Not pregnancy-only. Not mouse-only. Of the compartment pairings in this screen this is close to the least constrained one available. The gating constraint is the clonal mark, not tissue access, and even that has an existing human substrate: the lentiviral HSC gene-therapy cohort in PMID 39442556 (Nature 2024; 53 patients, MLD/WAS/beta-thalassaemia, integration sites as clonal identity, follow-up to 8 years, PB and BM). I read its Methods (archived at /home/user/aaa/refs/D3_PMC11618100.txt) and confirmed the relevant gap: NK cells were purified as BULK CD56+ by immunomagnetic beads ("CD56 + (CD56 Micro Beads Human, MILTENYI BIOTEC) were isolated in sequence"), with no bright/dim split anywhere in the study. So the human clonal substrate for this exact question exists and has already been banked longitudinally; what is missing is a FACS sort of bright vs dim in place of a bulk CD56 bead pull. Analogous human substrates: allo-HSCT genome-wide somatic-mutation clonal tracking (PMID 39478227). Optional compartments: (C) bone marrow needs an aspirate — a real but routine procedural gate in transplant/GT cohorts where marrow is already drawn; (D) tonsil is available as routine surgical waste, lymph node only at surgery. Neither is required for the core bright-vs-dim adjudication.
nearest_occupant: Two occupants, near-misses on orthogonal axes; neither adjudicates the claim. NEAREST OVERALL - PMID 36289449 (Ruckert et al., Nat Immunol 2022). Difference: right species (human), right compartments (blood CD56bright and CD56dim, both annotated in one dataset), right primitive (somatic mtDNA mutations as endogenous clonal barcodes), WRONG QUESTION. They asked whether adaptive NKG2C+ NK cells are clonal expansions and answered yes. Bright-vs-dim clone sharing was never tested as such; the only bearing on D3 is a one-sentence null observation that mtDNA clonotypes fail to associate with conventional-subset identity, glossed as marks "present already on the progenitor level." Critically their clonotype caller retains only clonotypes with a significantly enriched mutation and discards those defined by differential frequency of abundant mutations - it is built to detect expansions and by construction throws away the diffuse clonal structure a bright->dim test requires. So D3 is not pre-empted; it is one purpose-built reanalysis away from being addressable in public data (GEO GSE197037). NEAREST ON THE QUESTION ITSELF - PMID 30389798 (Wu et al., Sci Immunol 2018). Difference: asks precisely D3's structural question with lentiviral barcodes over >4 years and returns a clean NO - CD56-CD16+ NK clones stay clonally uncoupled from CD56+CD16- NK, and linear production from less mature CD56+CD16- cells is "negligible." But it is rhesus macaque, and the macaque axis is not the human one: macaque CD56+CD16- vs CD56-CD16+ maps onto human CD56bright vs CD56dim only by analogy, since human CD56dim are CD56-POSITIVE and CD16+. The species that carries the CD56bright/CD56dim partition (human) is the one where the clonal experiment has not been run, and the species where it has been run does not carry the partition. That mismatch is exactly why a primate clonal-grade answer already existing does not close the human claim.
crossfield_occupancy: HIGH occupancy of the STRUCTURAL question ("does phenotypically defined subset A give rise to subset B in vivo, adjudicated by clone sharing?"), across all three neighbouring fields - but zero occupancy of the human NK bright/dim instance. Importantly, the cross-field work reads as a validated TEMPLATE for D3 rather than a pre-emption of it, and it cuts against the linear-maturation reading twice. MYELOID - ANSWERED, IN HUMANS, WITH THE EXACT TOOL D3 WOULD USE. PMID 42242233 (Liu et al., Cancer Cell 2026, Mitotrek; preprint 40777278) used mtscATAC-seq + mtDNA clone calling on matched human tumor/tissue/blood to establish that TME-resident macrophages and DC3 are clonally related to circulating and tissue-infiltrating monocytes, and further resolved DC-biased vs macrophage-biased clones whose circulating precursors differ epigenetically. That is the monocyte->macrophage/DC arrow settled by clone sharing in human tissue - structurally identical to bright->dim, same primitive, same assay, same scale. It is a proof that the design works on a non-antigen-receptor-bearing innate compartment. Note the same senior authors (Ludwig, Lareau) are on Ruckert 2022, so the group that owns the tool has already touched human NK subsets and did not run this test. T CELL - ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER OVERTURNED THE LINEAR MODEL. The naive->effector->memory precursor-product question is the field's most heavily lineage-traced structure, via TCR sequences as free natural barcodes, mouse single-cell fate mapping, and human mtDNA (PMID 30827679, Ludwig et al., Cell 2019, the founding human mtDNA lineage-tracing paper; PMID 39123248 used X-inactivation-directed mtDNA to resolve human T clonal structure including gamma-delta separation; PMID 33037653 reviews T fate-mapping/lineage-tracing technologies specifically for CD8 subset generation). The substantive result is the cautionary one: clonal tools showed fate segregation of short-lived effector and long-lived memory progeny begins at or near the first division rather than by sequential maturation through a phenotypic ladder. Panjwani 2024 (PMID 39742279) transposes exactly this argument onto NK, invoking the naive-memory framework to argue CD56bright is a bipotential progenitor for classic-dim AND adaptive rather than a rung on a linear ladder. So the borrowed mechanism's occupancy does live in the field it was borrowed from, and there it demoted the linear reading. ILC / NK IN MODEL SPECIES - ANSWERED, ALSO AGAINST A SINGLE LINEAR ARROW. PMID 38872000 (Ding et al., Nat Immunol 2024) used mouse fate mapping to show NK cells arise by at least two developmental pathways - ENKP (NK-lineage-biased early progenitors) independent of the common ILC precursor ILCP - generating functionally distinct NK populations, which the authors suggest may be conserved in humans (see also review PMID 41634488). Combined with Wu 2018 in macaque, the two-independent-pools alternative to D3's arrow is the one that lineage tools have actually supported wherever they have been applied. NET: every adjacent field has run this experiment; two of them got answers that disfavour linear maturation; the human NK bright/dim instance is the conspicuous hole, and the tooling to fill it is demonstrated and public.

why: TRUE, with one scope condition and one design condition, both stated below. FORM. The claim is "the progeny of A are B" (A = conventional NKG2C-/FcRg+ NK; B = adaptive NK), not "A becomes functionally B-like". It is therefore in the decidable class — PROVIDED compartment B is operationalised as a SORT GATE (NKG2C+, and per Liu 2016 PMID 27117418 the NKG2C-independent adaptive gate: FcRg-/SYK-/CD57+/LILRB1+, demethylated IFNG CNS1) rather than as a function ("memory", "recall"). If B were defined by recall capacity, lineage could not decide it. Note the naming problem this exposes: NKG2C is dispensable (11/44 KLRC2-/- HCMV+ donors have bona fide adaptive expansions), so a barcoding study gated only on NKG2C would decide a narrower claim than the one the field actually holds. The gate must be the adaptive signature, not the receptor. WHY THE PRIMITIVE IS NOT TRIVIALLY SATISFIED. All NK cells in one person share an HSPC ancestor, so "do A and B share an ancestor?" is trivially YES and carries no information. The claim is decidable only through the RECENCY half of the primitive — which is exactly what the primitive supplies. The three live models make non-overlapping predictions about MRCA depth: (i) CONVERSION — an expanded adaptive clone's MRCA with a contemporaneous conventional NKG2C- cell sits at mature-NK depth, so one recent, NK-private clonotype contains both conventional and adaptive cells; (ii) SELECTION of a pre-existing already-NKG2C+ founder (Ruckert 2022's own stated model; Bjorkstrom 2011 PMC3023129; Adams 2019) — the adaptive clone's recent relatives are all already adaptive, and the MRCA with conventional NK sits only at progenitor depth; (iii) SEPARATE PROGENITOR (Bozzano 2021; Sci Adv 2025 thymic; cILC1 route PMID 42054258) — no sharing with the conventional NK pool even at NKP depth. Three distinguishable depth signatures; the tool is doing real work, not confirming a tautology. RECENCY CALIBRATION IS THE CRUX AND IS AVAILABLE. A shared mtDNA variant is informative only if progenitor-level origin can be excluded — Ruckert 2022 warns of precisely this ("mitochondrial mutations of conventional NK cells ... might instead be present already on the progenitor level"). The control is co-profiling autologous T/B/monocytes from the same draw: a variant also carried by unrelated lineages is progenitor-level; a variant private to NK and confined to a tight clone is recent. Feasibility precedent exists: PMID 42242233 (Cancer Cell 2026) reconstructs cross-compartment mtDNA clonal relationships across 218,715 cells from matched tumour/tissue/blood; PMID 38253266 (Nature 2024) does deep mtDNA detection with joint state readout. NOT A REVERSIBLE-STATE CLAIM (checked explicitly). The reversible-state exclusion does not fire here. The adaptive endpoint is a stably heritable epigenetic configuration (IFNG CNS1 demethylation, FCER1G/SYK/ZBTB16 silencing) that Ruckert 2022 shows persisting within the SAME mtDNA clonotypes over 7, 11 and 19 months; and Bjorkstrom 2011 reports the authors tested and could not induce NKG2C on NKG2C- cells. So it is not an oscillating state where both answers yield the same clonal structure. DESIGN CONDITION (the honest limit). The barcode alone locates the branch point but does not ORIENT it: a recent clonotype containing both conventional and adaptive cells is equally consistent with A->B, B->A, and a bifurcating common parent. Direction requires the longitudinal form of the same primitive — which clonotype carried which phenotype at t1 versus t2. A single cross-sectional timepoint decides branch DEPTH only; the directional arrow needs repeat sampling across the infection/expansion. Decidable, but only in the longitudinal design.
action_if_yes: YES = adaptive clones share recent, NK-private MRCAs with contemporaneous conventional NKG2C-/FcRg+ cells, and at the pre-expansion baseline the founder variant is carried by a phenotypically conventional cell. VERY NEXT EXPERIMENT: identify WHICH conventional NK cell is licensed to convert — a question the YES result poses and does not answer. Use the mtDNA clonotype as an index back into the baseline sample already in hand and read out the pre-conversion cell's own chromatin/surface state: CD56bright vs CD56dim, NKG2A+ vs KIR+, whether it is the CXXC5+ immature precursor nominated by PMC11686228 (Front Immunol 2024, which places an adaptive-NK precursor present at equal frequency in CMV+ and CMV- people), and critically whether KLRC2-locus accessibility or IFNG CNS1 demethylation is ALREADY partially present before infection (i.e. whether "conventional" founders are in fact pre-primed). Then convert descriptive to prospective: from an HCMV-seronegative donor, FACS-sort the nominated precursor gate versus its complement, and challenge in the autologous HCMV-infected fibroblast/monocyte coculture system (Guma 2006 / Rolle 2014 PMC4348979) or a humanised-mouse HCMV model, scoring adaptive output by the NKG2C-INDEPENDENT signature so the readout does not depend on the receptor Liu 2016 showed to be dispensable. This is the sort-the-precursor experiment nobody has run: Phase A records that no study anywhere purified an NKG2C-depleted conventional population and followed it for acquisition of the adaptive phenotype. TRANSLATIONAL CONSEQUENCE (different from the NO branch): conversion being real makes "adaptive" a MANUFACTURABLE STATE rather than a donor property. ADAPT-NK (Blood Adv 2022, PMC9628692) currently screens CMV-seropositive "superdonors" for large pre-existing adaptive subpopulations; under YES that screening step is an inefficiency to be engineered away, and the induction protocol — which conventional subset plus which signal — becomes the defined development target.
action_if_no: NO = adaptive clones' recent relatives are exclusively adaptive/NKG2C+; the MRCA with conventional NK appears only at progenitor depth (variant also present in autologous T/B/monocyte lineages); the pre-expansion baseline already carries the founder variant in an NKG2C+/adaptive-primed cell. VERY NEXT EXPERIMENT — and it is not the YES experiment, because NO leaves TWO sub-hypotheses standing that this dataset cannot separate: (a) the founder is a mature but already-adaptive-primed cell inside the conventional NK developmental stream, versus (b) the founder descends from a SEPARATE progenitor branch. Separating them requires acquiring a compartment the YES branch never needs: bone marrow aspirate (CD34+ HSPC, CLP, NKP, stage 3-4 NK precursors) plus the circulating Lin-CD34+DNAM-1bright CXCR4+ precursor of Bozzano 2021 (PMID 33493558) and circulating ILC1s (PMID 42054258), from the same individual, asking whether the adaptive founder clonotype maps to a progenitor branch distinct from the one feeding conventional NK. A positive result there promotes Bozzano 2021 / the Sci Adv 2025 thymic progenitor (PMID 40779632) from "alternative explanation" to "the actual origin". SECOND, PROSPECTIVE AND QUANTITATIVE: if the founder pool pre-exists, its SIZE and CLONAL DIVERSITY before infection should predict the magnitude and clonal composition of the post-infection expansion. Testable in a D+/R- transplant cohort with banked baseline draws, and it already has a human precedent to confirm or refute — Bjorkstrom 2011 (PMC3023129) found CMV-IgG-negative hantavirus patients had low baseline NKG2C+ numbers and never expanded despite identical acute viral insult. That is a pre-registered, falsifiable prediction, not a conclusion. TRANSLATIONAL CONSEQUENCE (opposite to YES): the problem stops being induction and becomes repertoire selection. Superdonor screening is then the correct irreducible design rather than a workaround, and the target shifts to identifying and sorting the founder pool in seronegative donors. Separately, the diagnostic use of NKG2C to call clonally restricted NK populations non-neoplastic (Mod Pathol 2026, PMID 41786213) rests on adaptive NK being a normal expansion of the conventional NK lineage and would need restating if the origin is a distinct progenitor.
compartments_needed: CORE (all four required for the primary readout): 1. Peripheral blood CONVENTIONAL NK — CD3-CD14-CD19-CD56+ NKG2C- FcRg+ sort gate. 2. Peripheral blood ADAPTIVE NK — NKG2C+ AND, per Liu 2016, the NKG2C-independent adaptive gate (FcRg-/SYK-/CD57+/LILRB1+). Gating on NKG2C alone decides a narrower claim than the field holds. 3. Autologous NON-NK leukocytes from the SAME draw (T, B, monocytes). Not optional garnish — this is the progenitor-depth calibrator. Without it a shared mtDNA variant cannot be assigned to "recent conversion" versus "inherited from a common HSPC", and the whole readout is uninterpretable (Ruckert 2022's own stated caveat). 4. A PRE-EXPANSION TIMEPOINT from the SAME individual (baseline PBMC before primary HCMV infection or before reactivation). Required for the DIRECTIONAL claim only; the branch-depth version can be run cross-sectionally. ADDITIONAL, ONLY IF THE ANSWER IS NO: 5. Bone marrow CD34+ HSPC / CLP / NKP / stage 3-4 NK precursors. 6. Circulating Lin-CD34+DNAM-1bright CXCR4+ precursors (Bozzano 2021) and circulating ILC1 (PMID 42054258) — both blood, so free. 7. Thymus (only to test the Sci Adv 2025 thymic-progenitor origin). 8. Secondary lymphoid organ NK (only to test the Blood 2025 "transitional precursor in SLO" model).
compartments_obtainable: YES for the core, and this is the unusual case in this screen where the two compartments are both in blood. Items 1-3 are three FACS gates on a SINGLE peripheral blood draw from one living human. No surgery, no post-mortem, no pregnancy, no mouse. Precedent that the paired sort plus mtDNA readout actually works on exactly these cells: Ruckert 2022 (PMC9663309) sorted NKG2C+ and NKG2C- NK 1:1 from the same donors and ran mtscATAC/ASAP-seq; PMID 42242233 (Cancer Cell 2026) resolved cross-compartment mtDNA clonal relationships across 218,715 cells from matched tumour, tissue and blood in the same patients; PMID 39236287 tracked mtDNA-marked populations at 0.1-1% frequency in post-HSCT clinical samples. THE CONSTRAINT THAT ACTUALLY BITES IS TIME, NOT TISSUE. Item 4 — the pre-expansion baseline — cannot be obtained opportunistically, because primary HCMV infection is unpredictable in healthy adults. It exists only where a baseline draw is banked by protocol: (a) D+/R- solid-organ transplant recipients (Lopez-Verges 2011's own design); (b) allo-HSCT/UCBT recipients with cryopreserved pre-transplant PBMC (precedent: PMC11686228, an MSKCC cohort of 267 HCT patients with protocolised weekly CMV monitoring from D14); (c) congenital/infant primary-infection cohorts. Of these, D+/R- SOT is the CLEAN one: in allo-HSCT the reconstituting NK cells arise de novo from grafted HSPC rather than from mature conventional NK, so the "A" being followed is a progenitor, not a conventional NK cell, and the arrow being tested silently changes. Lymphodepletion and immunosuppression are confounds in both. Item 5 (bone marrow) requires an aspirate — invasive but routine, obtainable from the same living human, easiest in patients already undergoing marrow sampling or in HSCT donors. Item 6 is free (blood). Item 7 THYMUS IS SURGICAL-ONLY (paediatric cardiac surgery) and in practice cannot be paired with an adult blood adaptive compartment from the same individual. Item 8 SLO NK is SURGICAL OR POST-MORTEM/deceased-donor only. None of 7-8 is needed for the primary readout; both sit behind the NO branch. UNVERIFIED FEASIBILITY ASSUMPTION, flagged rather than assumed: every banked baseline is cryopreserved, and mtscATAC-seq is a fixed-cell, intact-mitochondria protocol. The Nat Protoc method paper (PMID 36792778) covers primary haematopoietic cells and several cell-processing/flow workflows, but I did not confirm a validated cryopreserved-PBMC arm. Cryo-compatibility of the baseline samples must be verified at Phase C, not presumed.
nearest_occupant: PMID 36289449 — Ruckert T, et al. "Clonal expansion and epigenetic inheritance of long-lasting NK cell memory." Nat Immunol 2022 (PMC9663309). Same species (human), same virus (HCMV), same cell pair (NKG2C-/conventional vs NKG2C+/adaptive NK), same primitive (somatic mtDNA variants as endogenous barcodes read by mtscATAC/ASAP-seq). It is not merely adjacent — it is the same experiment class on the same claim. FOUR CONCRETE DIFFERENCES, each traceable to a specific line of their methods or results: 1. NO AUTOLOGOUS NON-NK CALIBRATOR (P1 compartment 3). Their methods magnetically DEPLETE CD3, CD14 and CD19 cells before sorting, then sort CD3-CD14-CD19-CD7+. T cells, B cells and monocytes are physically removed from the input. Consequently a mtDNA variant shared between a conventional and an adaptive NK cell cannot be assigned to recent conversion versus inheritance from a common HSPC. They say so themselves: conventional-NK mtDNA variants "might instead be present already on the progenitor level." P1's entire compartment 3 is the fix for the gap Ruckert names. 2. NO PRE-EXPANSION BASELINE (P1 compartment 4). Their longitudinal arm is three HCMV+ donors re-drawn at 7, 11 and 19 months — both timepoints are chronic, post-expansion. It establishes clone STABILITY, not clone ORIGIN. No pre-seroconversion or pre-reactivation sample exists in the dataset, so the directional claim "conventional becomes adaptive" is never put to a temporal clonal test. 3. DIRECTION IS EPIGENETIC INFERENCE, NOT CLONAL TOPOLOGY. Their conventional-origin argument runs: adaptive subclusters split into two groups whose differential accessibility correlates with the CD56bright/early-CD56dim vs CD56dim axis, therefore "possibly reflecting the cell of origin." That is residue-of-state reasoning, exactly the kind of inference clonal barcoding is supposed to replace. The primary clonal statistic they report is clonotype-to-subcluster association WITHIN adaptive; the cross-boundary shared-ancestor test is not the reported readout, and their conventional-compartment result is a null. 4. NARROWER ADAPTIVE GATE THAN THE FIELD HOLDS (P1 compartment 2). The sort is NKG2C+/NKG2C-. FcRg is intracellular and appears only in their flow panel (anti-FcERI gamma-FITC), never in the ADT panel or the sort logic; SYK is absent entirely. Their ADT panel does carry CD57 and CD85j/ILT2, so the Liu-2016 adaptive gate is partially recoverable post hoc, but it was not a sort gate. They noticed the problem incidentally — donor P1 subcluster 4 "likely represents an NKG2C- adaptive NK cell expansion" — and did not pursue it. Gating on NKG2C alone decides a strictly narrower claim than P1 states. NEAREST OCCUPANT THAT DOES HAVE THE CALIBRATOR: PMID 27903532 (Corat/Winkler, Blood 2017). It carries autologous neutrophils and CD56bright NK as internal clonal-depth references and answers the branch-depth half — the adaptive CD56dim/PLZF-negative pool is maintained independently of current HSPC output. It differs by being (a) bulk flow-percentage resolution of GPI-negativity per subset, not cell-by-cell shared-ancestor resolution, (b) restricted to PNH patients, a disease context with a clonally distorted HSPC pool, (c) blind to the conventional-NK-to-adaptive-NK step itself — PIGA marks HSPC descent, not intra-NK conversion, and (d) predating any NKG2C-independent adaptive gate. The residual unoccupied space is therefore narrow and specific: the calibrated, directional version of the question. Nobody has run mtDNA clonal tracing on conventional NK + adaptive NK + autologous T/B/monocytes from one draw, and nobody has a pre-expansion clonal baseline.
crossfield_occupancy: G4 applies — P1 invokes differentiation, plasticity and memory. All three neighbouring fields have answered the same structural question with lineage tools, and in two of them the answer is settled. T CELL FIELD — FULLY OCCUPIED, AND THIS IS WHERE THE METHOD WAS BORROWED FROM. "Is compartment B the progeny of compartment A" is decided routinely in T cells by the rearranged TCR, a perfect native heritable barcode: clonotype sharing between naive and memory compartments is measured directly (naive CD4/CD8 share ~5% and ~3.5% of TCRbeta clonotypes with their memory counterparts; overlap scales with clonotype frequency), and TCR-based clonal tracking maps permitted transitions between effector/memory subsets by ontogeny versus interconversion. The NK field's whole predicament is the absence of this native barcode, which is exactly why mtDNA is pressed into service as the surrogate. So P1 is not proposing a novel structural question — it is proposing to import the T cell field's settled question into a lineage that lacks the T cell field's barcode. Ruckert's own discussion makes the borrowing explicit ("As T cells can also clonally inherit transcriptional and epigenetic diversity..."). MYELOID FIELD — NOW OCCUPIED WITH THE IDENTICAL METHOD AND A BETTER COMPARTMENT DESIGN. why: This is the rubric's second bullet ("A becomes functionally B-like") in its purest form, compounded by the fourth (reversible/graded state within one lineage). Four independent reasons, in order of force. (1) B HAS NO LINEAGE-INDEPENDENT DEFINITION. "CIML NK" is scored by one thing only: enhanced IFN-gamma on restimulation. Cooper 2009 (PMC2644138) shows the cells are phenotypically indistinguishable from IL-15-only controls across CD69, CD11b, CD11c, gp49B, B220, CD122, IL-15Ralpha, IL-12Rbeta1 and CD127, are granzyme-B NEGATIVE, and kill YAC-1 no better ("all 4 groups of NK cells exhibited similar cytotoxicity"). So B is co-extensive with the assay used to define it. The barcoding primitive returns ancestry, not function; something else must still call a cell "B", and once the recall assay has called it, the barcode has added nothing to the claim's arrow. (2) THE CONVERSION STEP INVOLVES NO CELL DIVISION, SO IT WRITES NOTHING INTO THE GENEALOGY. The protocol is 13-16 h. Cooper 2009 Fig 4 is explicit that generation-0 (never-divided) preactivated cells make as much IFN-gamma as generations 1-3. Lineage structure is created by division. A transformation that occurs without division leaves the clonal tree of the population IDENTICAL before and after — under the conversion model AND under the selection model. "Do these two cells share an ancestor, and how recently" returns the same answer either way. There is no lineage signal to read because none was generated. (3) A AND B ARE UNCONTESTEDLY THE SAME LINEAGE. Nobody in this literature proposes that CIML NK cells are non-NK-derived; Keppel 2013 already excluded de novo endogenous NK development with Rag2-/-gc-/- hosts. The only lineage question with a live disagreement — donor vs host — is a two-population question already settled by CD45.1/CD45.2 congenics in mouse, which needs no clonal resolution at all. (4) THE REAL DISPUTE (SELECTION vs CONVERSION) IS NOT A CLONAL QUESTION. The hypothesized pre-existing responsive compartment is a DIFFERENTIATION STAGE — CD56bright/NKG2A+/CD57-/KIR- in Romee 2012's own marker correlations, CD27hi in mouse — not a clone. Its members are distributed across clonotypes. So "selection of that subset" and "conversion of everything" both predict a broad, essentially unbiased clonotype draw. Both answers are consistent with the same clonal structure, which is exactly the rubric's disqualifying condition. Add that the state is reversible and dose/duration-graded (5 h gives a weaker effect than overnight; Keppel 2013 concedes in print it "could represent a residual priming effect, rather than a memory-like response"), so "converted then decayed" and "never converted" are also clonally identical. STRONGEST COUNTER-CONSIDERATION, AND WHY IT DOES NOT RESCUE DECIDABILITY. There is one genuinely lineage-shaped design: barcode a proliferating NK pool, split sibling cells into preactivation vs control, and ask whether recall competence is concordant within a barcode (clone-intrinsic, i.e. pre-existing) or uncorrelated (induced). That is the primitive used correctly. But it requires clones with multiple members, which requires 10-14 days of feeder/IL-2 expansion at 300-450 fold to manufacture — precisely what Allan/Dunbar 2023 (PMID 36699615, PMC9842935) did in barcoded rhesus macaques, finding correlated clone-intrinsic proliferative behaviour across two feeder conditions (Pearson r 0.52-0.67). Running that design replaces the claim's 16 h no-division protocol with a fortnight of driven proliferation, i.e. you must change the biology to make it lineage-legible. It answers a different claim.

why: FALSE on four independent grounds, any one of which is sufficient. (1) WRONG PREDICATE. The claim's predicate is a function — % specific 51Cr release on 721.221/K562, % conjugates with polarized MTOC and perforin at 20 min, CD107a exposure. The primitive returns shared-ancestry and nothing else. This is verbatim the "A becomes functionally B-like" form that prereg 3 fixes as not decidable. Phase A already recorded is_lineage_claim=FALSE: no clone, barcode, congenic marker, transfer, fate map or recorder appears anywhere in Kopcow 2005, Verma 2000, Tokmadzic 2002, El Costa 2008 or Siewiera 2013. (2) THE ANSWER IS FIXED BY CONSTRUCTION, SO IT CANNOT COVARY WITH THE CLAIM. The two things compared are one bead-purified dNK population at t=0 and the same dish at 36 h. They are trivially co-lineal — one prep, one tube. The primitive's output is known before the experiment is run, so it carries zero information about whether the claim is true. A test whose result is determined by the sampling scheme rather than by the hypothesis is not a test. (3) REVERSIBLE STATE WITHIN ONE LINEAGE — the decisive point. Cytotoxic competence here is an environmentally-set, reversible functional state, and Kopcow's own Discussion says so verbatim: "the immunosuppressive environment of the decidua might be responsible for blocking MTOC and granule polarization. Regain of cytotoxicity may result from the removal of dNK from this environment." At least three mutually exclusive readings — (a) IL-15 induces the state, (b) leaving the decidua de-represses it, (c) it was never absent (El Costa 2008 PMID 18713971: fresh uncultured dNK lyse after NKp46 crosslinking; Siewiera 2013 PMID 23592985: fresh dNK kill autologous HCMV-infected decidual fibroblasts) — all produce the IDENTICAL clonal structure. Every truth-value of the claim maps to the same barcode distribution, so the barcode distribution cannot discriminate among them. That is the definition of not decidable. (4) OPERATIONAL DEGENERACY. Over the 12-36 h window purified dNK essentially do not divide, so no two cells acquire a shared recent ancestor during the experiment; the primitive collapses to per-cell tagging and returns "no shared ancestor" for every pair whether or not the claim holds. Extending culture until clones do arise substitutes a different experiment, since long culture is itself the confound being adjudicated. Compounding this, barcoding primary human NK requires activating transduction culture (cf. barcoded lentiviral NK delivery, PMID 40621477), which imposes the exact ex vivo perturbation at issue — the instrument creates the artefact it is meant to measure. The one sub-question lineage could in principle touch — selection of a pre-existing competent minority versus conversion of each cell — is NOT the claim as written, and would additionally require functionally phenotyping the ancestor, which the chromium-release assay consumes.

Cytokine-driven, REVERSIBLE inter-state conversion (NKp46+ ILC3 <-> ILC1, ILC2 -> ILC1/ILC3, driven by IL-12/IL-18 and Notch, reversing on cytokine withdrawal) was established with genetic fate mappers (Rorc fate-mapped "ex-ILC3", T-bet fate mapping) precisely because flow phenotype alone could not distinguish "converted" from "recruited." T CELL — occupied for the same structure. TCR clonotype is a free endogenous clonal barcode and the field has used it to show that progenitor-exhausted and terminally exhausted, and circulating and tissue-resident, states are routinely occupied by the SAME clone (e.g. PMID 41308653, "Deep profiling of human T cells defines compartmentalized clones and phenotypic trajectories across blood and tonsils," 2025; PMID 34127056, "Maintenance of the human memory T cell repertoire by subset and tissue site," Genome Med 2021). NET: the mechanism R1 borrows has had its clonal structure resolved in three adjacent fields, and in all three the clonal answer was "same lineage, different state" — the outcome B1 flags as non-discriminating. why: R3 asserts no ancestry relation. There is no compartment A and compartment B whose relatedness is in question — the subject is one population of human blood NK cells in one well, sampled at day 7 (TGF-beta on) and day 17 (10 days after washout). Taking the two halves separately: (ii) "effector function does not revert" is a pure function claim, read out as granzyme A/B and IFN-gamma expression and (elsewhere in the source) target killing. The primitive returns only whether two cells share an ancestor and how recently. It is silent on whether either cell can degranulate or make IFN-gamma. NOT DECIDABLE, categorically. (i) "residency phenotype reverts" is the textbook REVERSIBLE STATE WITHIN ONE LINEAGE. CD103/CD9/CD49a switching on and off leaves no trace in the genealogy: whether the marker reverts or persists, the same clones are present at day 17, descended from the same day-0 founders, with the same coalescent structure. Both answers are consistent with an identical barcode readout, so the barcode cannot discriminate them. The one genuinely lineage-shaped residue is the selection-vs-conversion alternative: are the day-17 marker-negative cells the PROGENY of the day-7 CD103+ cells (true reversion), or the outgrowth of clones that were never CD103+ (selection)? That is a legitimate "same/different lineage" question and IS decidable in principle. But it is not what the claim asserts, it addresses only the trivial half, and a definitive answer either way leaves the load-bearing assertion — persistence of the functional deficit — completely untouched. Overall verdict FALSE.
action_if_yes: Design that produces a YES: barcode human PB NK cells at day 0 (lentiviral barcoding of human/rhesus NK is established — PMID 40621477, PMID 31649681), expose to TGF-beta, index-sort CD103+ cells at day 7, withdraw, re-read barcodes plus surface phenotype at day 17. YES = the day-17 CD103-negative cells carry the SAME barcodes as the day-7 CD103+ cells, i.e. within-clone reversion, no selective outgrowth. Very next experiment after YES: nothing lineage-shaped is left to do. You would immediately have to run the non-lineage experiment the claim actually turns on — is the effector deficit a slower RECOVERY TIME CONSTANT or genuine signal-independent fixity? That means (a) withdrawal arms beyond a single 10-day timepoint (20/30/40 d), (b) CellTrace/CFSE division tracking to match proliferative history between arms, since TGF-beta durably suppressed Ki67 and dilution-through-division is exactly the mechanism that resets chromatin and protein load, (c) a TGF-betaR inhibitor arm at withdrawal to prove the signal is truly off, (d) a cytotoxicity readout in the day-17 withdrawal arm (the source has none), and (e) the field-standard test from T cell exhaustion (Philip 2017, PMID 28514453): transfer the withdrawn cells OUT of the inducing environment in vivo and show the state survives multiple rounds of division. None of these requires or uses the barcode.
action_if_no: NO = the day-17 marker-negative population is dominated by barcodes that were CD103-negative at day 7, i.e. apparent "reversion" is selective outgrowth of never-converted clones rather than a cell changing state. Very next experiment after NO: the identical experiment listed under YES. You would rewrite one sentence about marker kinetics and then still have to run the longer withdrawal timecourse, division tracking, inhibitor arm, killing assay and in vivo removal to learn whether the effector deficit is fixed — because the effector half of the claim is untouched by the selection finding, and a selection result does not predict its direction. This branch is additionally close to foreclosed and close to vacuous. The source already ran the population-level version of exactly this control (Fig. S3A-C): CD103+ and CD103- NK cells were sorted at day 7 and recultured separately, and BOTH lost CD103 after withdrawal. A barcode experiment returning NO would have to overturn an existing purification control, and if it did, it would revise only a footnote about marker lability that is in any case established better, peer-reviewed and in vivo in humans elsewhere (Niehrs, Nat Immunol 2025, PMID 41087727).
compartments_needed: AS REGISTERED (human, in vitro), there is no compartment pair — A and B are the same culture at two timepoints: A = day-7 TGF-beta-exposed human PB NK cells (CD103+/CD9+/CD49a+ fraction, FACS-sortable) B = day-17 NK cells from the same well, 10 days after washout C = day-17 IL-15-only NK cells from the same donor (required handling-matched control) All three are splits of one negatively-enriched NK prep from a single venipuncture of one healthy adult. That selection-vs-reversion distinction is precisely and only what clonal barcoding could add, and nobody has added it. NEAREST ON METHOD (lineage tool, adjacent question): PMID 41966330 (Mucosal Immunol 2026) "Eomes fate-labeling reveals a subset of Eomes-lo NK cells that exhibits an ILC1-like phenotype." This is structurally the closest lineage adjudication that exists: it uses an irreversible label to prove that cells displaying the residency/ILC1-like surface phenotype are fate-labelled ex-Eomes NK cells, i.e. a STATE change inside one lineage rather than a lineage switch — the same "is this a reversible state or a different lineage" question R3 sits on. why: TRUE, but only under one of the two readings the claim conflates, and the row must be re-worded to that reading or it is not decidable at all. (a) DECIDABLE READING — persistence/identity across time: "the NK cells present in the uterus after delivery are the same clones as (or clonal descendants of) the dNK present during that pregnancy." This is a straight "A and B are the same lineage / the progeny of A are B" proposition. The primitive answers it directly: sample dNK at t1 and uterine NK at t2 in the same woman, ask whether t2 cells fall into clones containing t1 cells and how recently they shared an ancestor. YES = overlapping clones with recent common ancestry; NO = disjoint clones. These are genuinely different clonal structures, so the primitive discriminates. (b) NOT DECIDABLE READING — the claim's own label: "PTdNK" in the source means Pregnancy-Trained dNK, i.e. dNK acquire an NKG2C-hi/LILRB1-hi epigenetically imprinted state that makes them secrete more IFN-g and VEGFa in a subsequent pregnancy. That is function and phenotype causation, which lineage does not measure. It is also a marker-state claim, and any clone can occupy or vacate a marker state, so both answers are consistent with the same clonal structure. Phase A already flagged this conflation (the lineage half is what R4 asserts and has no evidence; the functional half has evidence and is not what R4 asserts). NOT the reversible-state failure mode: R4 sits in the registry's "reversal" group but is not a reversibility claim — persistence is about physical presence of cells over time, not about a state occupied and vacated. Phase A flagged the group label as a category error and I concur. RESOLUTION LIMIT that must be carried forward: shared mtDNA variants between t1 dNK and t2 uterine NK establish common ancestry, not survival of the individual cells. A marrow clone that seeds the uterus twice produces the same signature as a cell that stayed put. Contemporaneous blood at both timepoints is therefore not an optional control — it is the only thing that converts "shared ancestry" into "local persistence." The decidable proposition is strictly "the postpartum uterine NK pool is drawn from the same, uterus-restricted clones as the pregnancy dNK pool," not "the individual cells survived."

Next experiment: add a THIRD timepoint — decidua from that same woman's subsequent pregnancy — and ask whether the clones retained postpartum are the ones that dominate and expand in the next pregnancy, which is the source's actual model. Why this branch is weaker than it looks: the obvious follow-up ("are the persisting clones the ones carrying the NKG2C-hi / trained chromatin state?") is NOT a next experiment — mtscATAC-seq yields clone identity and chromatin accessibility from the same cells, so that intersection falls out of the very run that produced the YES. It is the adjudicating experiment's second panel. The only genuinely new experiment is the subsequent-pregnancy timepoint: the same assay again, years later, contingent on that woman conceiving and on tissue access at the next termination or delivery (see B3, compartment 4). Payoff is further compressed by Gamliel's own Fig 1G — the NKG2C-hi expansion is present at gravidity>=2 with parity 0, i.e. it tracks having been pregnant, not having delivered — so a YES on post-delivery persistence would not vindicate the source's model either.
action_if_no: NO = the postpartum uterine NK repertoire is clonally disjoint from the pregnancy dNK and is a fresh draw from the contemporaneous blood repertoire. Next experiment: there is none that the adjudicating experiment has not already performed. The blood arm is mandatory in the design (it is what makes YES interpretable at all), so "they came from the circulation" is already in hand from the same data the moment NO is returned. The NO answer opens nothing new. The only residual move is to relocate the "memory" from the NK cell to the endometrial niche — ask whether postpartum stroma/epithelium carries the mark and imprints freshly recruited NK (stromal ATAC/methylation, endometrial organoid plus naive NK co-culture). That is (i) a change of subject away from lineage entirely, (ii) an unbounded "go look somewhere else" rather than a determinate next step, and (iii) already the standing model, and it lands in territory this screen holds as T3/T5 (blood NK -> dNK-like in vitro; glycodelin-A). compartments_needed: Four, of which three must be paired within one woman across two timepoints: 1. dNK from an ONGOING PREGNANCY (t1). Available only during pregnancy and only at a procedure: first-trimester decidua at elective surgical termination (the Gamliel/Hadassah route), or term decidua basalis at Caesarean section / from the basal plate of a delivered placenta. Never obtainable non-invasively. 2. UTERINE LINING AFTER DELIVERY (t2). Four imperfect routes: (i) lochia / shed decidua in the first postpartum days — non-invasive, but it is the EXPELLED material, degraded and blood-admixed, and measures what is being shed rather than what is retained; (ii) Pipelle endometrial biopsy at >=3 months postpartum — feasible, research-only, invasive, requires endometrial regeneration; (iii) menstrual blood by menstrual cup once cycles resume — non-invasive, this is Gamliel's "eNK" compartment, but return of menses is delayed months by lactation and the sample is again shed, not retained, endometrium; (iv) hysterectomy specimen — rare and confounded by the pathology prompting it. 3. CONTEMPORANEOUS PERIPHERAL BLOOD AT BOTH t1 AND t2. Trivially obtainable and strictly mandatory — the only way to separate local persistence from re-seeding by a clone that also lives in blood/marrow (see B1 resolution limit). 4. (Only to test the source's actual model) DECIDUA FROM THE SAME WOMAN'S SUBSEQUENT PREGNANCY (t3). Requires her to conceive again and to have tissue access at that pregnancy.
compartments_obtainable: PARTIALLY YES — compartments 1+2+3 are genuinely obtainable paired from one human; compartment 4 is not, at any usable n. OBTAINABLE PAIRED (1+2+3): a prospective design works — term decidua plus blood at Caesarean section, then Pipelle biopsy or menstrual-cup collection plus blood at 6-12 months postpartum, from the same woman. Costs are real but survivable: multi-month follow-up, cohort attrition, and IRB approval for a research endometrial biopsy in a postpartum woman. Nothing here is post-mortem-only and nothing is mouse-only. NOT OBTAINABLE (4): the subsequent-pregnancy sample cannot be scheduled — it needs the woman to conceive again years later AND to have surgical or obstetric tissue access at that pregnancy. It is also self-selecting in a way that breaks the comparison: a woman whose next pregnancy also ends in elective termination is a particular population, and a woman who delivers at term yields term decidua, which is not comparable to first-trimester decidua. This is the compartment the YES branch's only new experiment depends on, and it is the practical reason the YES branch cannot be closed out. TIMING CONSTRAINTS, explicitly: compartment 1 exists ONLY during pregnancy and only at a procedure. Compartment 2 exists either in the immediate postpartum window (lochia, degraded) or after a months-long delay (biopsy/menses, lactation-dependent). Neither compartment requires post-mortem access; neither is mouse-only.

why: The claim has two separable readings and only the weaker one is a lineage question. (a) "dNK1/dNK2/dNK3 are the same or different lineages" would be DECIDABLE (template 3). (b) "a differentiation ORDERING exists among them" — a directed arrow, e.g. dNK3->dNK2->dNK1 — is what the claim actually asserts, and it is NOT decidable from the primitive. Three reasons. (1) REVERSIBLE, MILIEU-INSTRUCTED STATE WITHIN ONE LINEAGE. The subset labels are graded surface/transcriptional states that the decidual environment sets and that are demonstrably inducible on the timescale of the assay itself: in Guo 2021 (PMID 33390590) CD39 — the marker that defines dNK1 in Guo's own ATAC sorting gate — is acquired within 2 days of culture by cells that lacked it; Huhn 2020 (PMID 31959757) CyTOF shows Eomes/T-bet as intermediate/graded across dNK1/2/3, not binary; Cheung 2026 (PMID 41999228) shows TGF-beta instructing dNK2-vs-dNK3 marker composition from a pluripotent source. Under "an ordering exists" and under "no ordering — three interconvertible, signal-instructed states of one decidual NK lineage", the PREDICTED CLONAL STRUCTURE IS IDENTICAL: clones spanning all three subsets. Both answers are consistent with the same clonal structure, which is exactly the reversible-state carve-out. (2) SHARED ANCESTRY CARRIES NO DIRECTION. "Share an ancestor and how recently" yields a tree; painting subset labels on its tips gives a direction ONLY under the added assumption that the label is heritable and transitions are rare or irreversible — precisely the assumption in dispute. With reversible labels, dNK2->dNK1 at rate r and dNK1->dNK2 at rate r' combined with differential proliferation generate the same tree. The topology is not identifiable, and there are three published mutually contradictory topologies to choose among. (3) SINGLE TERMINAL TIMEPOINT. Decidua is destructively sampled once per pregnancy, so "how recently" cannot be anchored to real time or to a second observation of the same clone, and subset frequencies shift with gestational age through differential proliferation/recruitment/attrition — which changes subclone sizes with zero cells changing identity. EMPIRICAL CONFIRMATION OF THE LIMIT: the only study to put DNA barcodes on human NK subsets (Vo et al. 2024, PMID 38484189; CellTag lentiviral barcoding of CD34+ progenitors, progeny sorted into ILC3 / S3b-NK / S4-NK) concluded verbatim "clonal bias was only observed between ILC3 and NK cell subsets but not within the NK cell stages." Reading (a) succeeded and reading (b) went flat, in the same experiment, with the same tool.
action_if_yes: DESIGN BEING ADJUDICATED: mtscATAC-seq / MAESTER on hashed, FACS-sorted dNK1 (CD39+CD18-CD103-), dNK2 (CD18+CD39-CD103-) and dNK3 (CD18+CD103+) from a single first-trimester decidua, asking whether somatic mtDNA clones are shared across the three subsets. YES = clones are shared; the three subsets sit inside common recent clades. NEXT EXPERIMENT: precisely the one you would run with no lineage data at all — a directional/perturbation experiment to supply the arrow the barcodes do not contain. Concretely: a gestational-age series (6->14 wk) with subset composition tracked, plus decidual explant or endometrial-organoid co-culture with TGF-beta / IL-15 / HLA-C-KIR-ligand manipulation, re-phenotyping on the FULL multi-marker dNK1 identity (KIR, LILRB1, granzyme/perforin, glycolytic programme) rather than CD39 alone. Nothing about the barcode result changes which perturbation you run, which of the three contradictory published topologies you favour, or how you read the outcome. WHY THIS ARM IS VACUOUS: YES is the near-certain a priori outcome. dNK contain an overt proliferating cluster (dNKp) in both Vento-Tormo 2018 and Guo 2021, and mouse uterine trNK accumulate by LOCAL proliferation with no contribution from migrating NK (Sojka 2018, PMID 30275046). A locally expanded compartment whose states are milieu-set will share clones across states — that is the prediction before any experiment. Confirming it moves nothing.
action_if_no: NO = the three subsets are clonally disjoint; no mtDNA clone spans dNK1/dNK2/dNK3. NEXT EXPERIMENT: this would refute the ordering outright, and the follow-up is to chase each subset's separate origin using the same mtDNA variants — match dNK1/2/3 clonotypes against paired maternal peripheral-blood NK drawn at the same procedure, and against pre-pregnancy endometrium if any is available, to ask whether each subset is separately seeded from the circulation or separately maintained in situ. WHY THIS ARM IS WEAK RATHER THAN VACUOUS: (i) it is the same assay extended to one additional compartment, not a different kind of experiment; (ii) the NO result is close to unreachable with this primitive, because absence of shared mtDNA clones is an UNDERPOWERED NULL — it is governed by how many informative heteroplasmies that particular donor carries, capture depth, and cells recovered per subset, and there is no calibration for what clone-sharing "should" look like in a polyclonal, locally expanded decidual NK pool. A null therefore reads "not enough informative variants", whose follow-up is "repeat the assay with more variants/cells", i.e. the same experiment again.
compartments_needed: INDEX COMPARTMENTS (all three required simultaneously): dNK1, dNK2 and dNK3 from the SAME first-trimester decidua (6-14 gestational weeks), sorted on the published gates (dNK1 CD39+CD18-CD103-; dNK2 CD18+CD39-CD103-; dNK3 CD18+CD103+), ideally with the proliferating dNKp fraction retained as the within-tissue clonal anchor. REFERENCE COMPARTMENTS (required only for the NO arm / origin question): paired maternal peripheral-blood NK from the same woman at the same procedure; pre-pregnancy (or non-pregnant) endometrium from the same woman; a bone-marrow / NK-precursor compartment from the same woman.
compartments_obtainable: PARTIAL — the index compartments are trivially co-obtainable; every reference compartment is not. OBTAINABLE PAIRED FROM ONE HUMAN: dNK1 + dNK2 + dNK3 all live in a single cell suspension from one decidual specimen, so the "compartment A and B simultaneously from the same individual" requirement is met better here than for almost any other claim in this screen. This is S1's one genuine strength. Paired maternal peripheral blood is routinely drawn at the same procedure (Vento-Tormo 2018 used 6 matched blood donors). ONLY AT SURGERY, AND ONLY DURING PREGNANCY: first-trimester decidua is obtained only at elective surgical termination — or by D&C after embryo demise, which is the disease arm and not a control. The specimen is terminal for that individual: one timepoint per woman, no re-sampling, no follow-up, no before/after within a subject. This is what removes the time axis the ordering claim needs. NOT OBTAINABLE: pre-pregnancy endometrium from the SAME woman who later supplies the decidua (would require a prospective biopsy in a woman who subsequently conceives and terminates — vanishingly rare); bone marrow or any NK-precursor compartment from the same pregnant woman. Post-mortem access is neither required nor useful here. NOT AVAILABLE IN MOUSE: dNK1/2/3 is a human-only taxonomy resting on KIR and LILRB1 and on HLA-C/HLA-G engagement. Mice have no KIR and no HLA-G; mouse uterine NK are classified DBA-lectin+/- (PMID 22875907). The most recent mouse decidual fate-mapping study (PMID 41782473, Rosa26-RFP x Tbx21-Cre across gestation) itself attributes dNK1/2/3 to human scRNA-seq and never assigns them in mouse. So the one species where a genetic clonal recorder (Confetti, Polylox, CRISPR recorder) could be deployed does not contain the entities the claim is about.
nearest_occupant: NEAREST OCCUPANT (same tissue, same ordering question, different primitive): Strunz et al. 2021, Sci Immunol, PMID 33617461 — "Continuous human uterine NK cell differentiation in response to endometrial regeneration and pregnancy." They assert exactly an ordering: a sequential uNK differentiation pathway with stepwise acquisition of KIR then CD39, driven by IL-15, coupled to endometrial regeneration; differentiated uNK show reduced proliferative capacity and enhanced angiogenic function. Ordering is inferred from marker co-expression, phenotype gradients and bulk reconstitution kinetics — never from whether two cells share an ancestor. Nothing in it can distinguish "dNK2 is the parent of dNK1" from "dNK1 and dNK2 are independently seeded and merely co-vary with tissue state." (b) Different axis. Strunz's axis is KIR-/CD39- -> KIR+/CD39+. That partially overlaps the dNK1 gate (CD39+) but leaves CD18 and CD103 — the coordinates that separate dNK2 from dNK3 — entirely unaddressed. The three published gates (dNK1 CD39+CD18-CD103-; dNK2 CD18+CD39-CD103-; dNK3 CD18+CD103+) are never jointly resolved. (c) The uterus-transplant and humanized-mouse data answer the ORIGIN/replenishment question (uNK niche is refilled from circulation, and is under genetic control) at the population level. That is the NO-arm reference question of this claim, not the within-tissue ordering — and it is answered by donor/recipient chimerism, a binary origin label, not by clonal ancestry.
