why: DECIDABLE in its pool-level form, with a large and explicitly stated undecidable residue that covers the claim's numbered indices. The claim has to be split, because its two halves fall on opposite sides of the rubric. (i) DECIDABLE HALF — POOL-LEVEL CARRIAGE. "The decidual uNK pool is the progeny of the pre-conception endometrial uNK pool" is the rubric's "the progeny of A are B" form, and — more decisively — its live rival is itself a PURE CLONAL-STRUCTURE statement, so the fork is exactly what the primitive returns and essentially nothing else in human can settle it. The two rivals are both on the record and both supported by evidence of a stronger class than the claim's own INF_MARKER. Carriage: Sojka 2018 (PMID 30275046), mouse Ncr1 reporter + parabiosis + induced deciduoma — "the accumulated uNK cells were proliferating trNK cells; migrating NK cells made no contribution." Re-recruitment: Greene 2025 (PMID 40672293) — "uNKs derive from circulatory cells in the peripheral blood which immigrate into the endometrium and become resident as they reconstitute the uterine lining after menses"; Strunz 2026 (PMID 41811987), SNP-demultiplexed uterus transplant — "recipient-derived immune cells replaced donor immune cells after uterus transplant"; Tatematsu & Sojka 2025 (PMID 39708955), parabiosis — uterine trNK "are derived from peripheral cNK cells" under progesterone control. Choosing between these is asking whether a decidual NK cell shares a recent ancestor with a pre-conception endometrium-resident NK cell or only with the contemporaneous circulating pool. Ancestor-sharing plus recency, nothing else. The "HOW RECENTLY" clause is load-bearing, not decorative. Every NK cell in one woman shares an HSPC ancestor, so bare ancestor-sharing is trivially TRUE under both models. The discriminating readout is whether the decidual repertoire is a low-diversity, bottlenecked subsample of the woman's PRIOR endometrial repertoire (carriage + local expansion) or an unbiased sample of her CONTEMPORANEOUS blood repertoire (recruitment). Note also that the negative is the decisive direction: clonal discordance between prior endometrium and later decidua, against a blood baseline, falsifies carriage outright. (ii) NOT DECIDABLE — THE NUMBERED 1:1 ARROW uNK1->dNK1, uNK2->dNK2, uNK3->dNK3. This is the rubric's reversible-state case and it fails for the stated reason: both answers are consistent with the same clonal structure. uNK1/2/3 are gated on CD39/CD103/CD49a/KIR/LILRB1 — inducible surface molecules, not heritable marks. Strunz 2021 (PMID 33617461) reports a CONTINUUM with sequential KIR-then-CD39 acquisition driven by IL-15; Greene 2025 attributes the divergent subsets to differential TGF-beta responsiveness of blood-derived precursors AFTER they immigrate; and Cheung 2025 (PMID 41279445 / PMC12637421) derives dNK1/2/3-like subtypes de novo from induced pluripotent stem cells, i.e. the three states are reachable from a starting cell that has never been in a uterus. Consequence: a barcode shared between an endometrial uNK1 and a decidual dNK1 is produced equally by (a) a uNK1 cell carried forward retaining its state, (b) a carried clone of any state re-differentiating into the dNK1 state under local TGF-beta/IL-15, or (c) one clone spanning all three states. Lineage cannot order or attribute a state that is re-inducible from outside the compartment, so the subset indices are not adjudicable by this primitive. One sub-question inside (ii) IS decidable and should be separated out rather than conflated: "are uNK1/2/3 three separate lineages or three states of one lineage?" — clonal confinement versus clonal sharing across the three gates is the rubric's explicit same/different-lineage case. But answering it does not rescue the arrow; it only reports whether the numbering denotes lineages at all. And Phase A found the gates themselves may not be stable entities to test: Whettlock's own term decidual uNK form ONE cluster when analysed alone and three only after integration with the other datasets, and Guo 2024 recovers a different partition on identical markers. NET: TRUE, because the load-bearing scientific fork this claim actually turns on (carriage vs re-recruitment) is a clonal-structure question and this primitive is definitionally competent to settle it. The claim should be carried forward only in its rewritten pool-level form; the "1/2/3" indices must be dropped from anything that goes to Phase C, because they are not decidable. PRACTICAL CAVEAT, recorded here but not allowed to flip B1 (which is about in-principle decidability): the only human-usable mark is endogenous, and NK cells have no rearranged receptor to serve as an endogenous clonal marker — Wu 2022 (PMID 36605190) says this explicitly and is why lentiviral barcodes were needed in macaque. So the human readout must be mtDNA variants (mtscATAC/MAESTER) or somatic mutation, whose discriminating power scales with prior clonal expansion. That is a Phase C power question, not a decidability question.
action_if_yes: IF YES — decidual NK clones descend from clones that were resident in the endometrium BEFORE conception, at a sharing rate above the same woman's blood baseline. TWO CONCRETE NEXT EXPERIMENTS, neither of which is the adjudicating experiment repeated. (1) MECHANISTIC, AND THE ONE I WOULD DO FIRST — locate the reservoir that survives menstruation. Carriage across a conception is only possible if some uNK clones persist through the shedding of the functionalis, and the immediate unanswered question becomes WHERE. Design: serial clonal census of menstrual effluent from the SAME woman across >=3 consecutive cycles, with a paired peripheral blood draw each cycle. Menstrual effluent is a validated source of uterine NK with a KIR repertoire markedly distinct from blood (PMID 27271316), and it is non-invasive, so serial within-woman sampling is actually possible here in a way it is not for biopsy. Readout: do the same clones reappear cycle after cycle (a persistent reservoir reseeding each regenerated functionalis) or is each cycle's uNK repertoire clonally fresh and blood-derived (in which case carriage across a pregnancy must run through some non-functionalis compartment, and the basalis becomes the target)? Different compartment, different timescale, non-pregnant subjects — and a question that is only worth asking once carriage is established. (2) TRANSLATIONAL, WITH A DIFFERENT ENDPOINT — power the clinical test whose premise this claim silently is. Pre-conception mid-luteal endometrial uNK assays are already being run and cut-offs already published (PMID 36592442, PMID 25150956, PMID 38164429), and Woon 2022 (PMID 36713400) reasons explicitly from pre-conception endometrial uNK1/2/3 to what will happen to extravillous trophoblast in a later pregnancy. If carriage holds, that inference is legitimate and the next experiment is the prospective cohort that has never been run: recruit in recurrent-miscarriage / recurrent-implantation-failure clinics where the biopsy is happening anyway, clone-census it, follow to live birth, and test whether CLONE-LEVEL structure of the pre-conception pool (clonal diversity, size of the clones that get carried, KIR genotype of the carried fraction) predicts outcome better than the current frequency/percentage readout. Endpoint = live birth, measured quantity = clonal, neither of which appears in the adjudicating experiment.
action_if_no: IF NO — decidual NK cells are clonally unrelated to the woman's own pre-conception endometrial pool, and instead nest inside her contemporaneous circulating repertoire. This branch is NOT "conclude the model is wrong and move on," because a NO answer LOCALIZES the source, and three mutually exclusive candidate sources are already named in this literature and are all sortable at a single surgical event. CONCRETE NEXT EXPERIMENT — the multi-compartment source-hunt, run cross-sectionally at one termination or caesarean, from one woman: clonal census of decidua basalis, decidua parietalis, adjacent non-decidualized endometrium, decidua-resident CD34+/stage-3 NK precursors (Vacca 2011, PMID 21248224, per the Phase A adversarial pass), and contemporaneous peripheral blood. Ask which compartment's clone set the decidual NK cells sit inside. Three distinguishable outcomes, each with a different follow-on: (a) decidual clones = contemporaneous blood NK clones -> recruitment of circulating NK, and the target for any pre-conception assay moves to blood; (b) decidual clones nest inside the decidual CD34+ precursor clones and NOT inside blood NK clones -> in-situ differentiation from a resident progenitor, and the compartment to profile and to perturb is the progenitor, not the NK cell; (c) decidual clones match neither -> the source is the unsampled basalis, which tells you the sampling scheme, not the biology, was wrong. Note this is a different DESIGN from the adjudicating experiment — single-timepoint, multi-compartment, cross-sectional, no pre-conception arm — not the same experiment rerun. SECOND, DIRECTLY CONSEQUENTIAL ACTION: a NO answer says the pre-conception endometrial uNK assay currently in clinical use is measuring a compartment that is discarded before the pregnancy it claims to predict. The next experiment is then the head-to-head assay-replacement study — does a blood-based precursor census (whatever compartment (a)/(b) identifies) outperform the mid-luteal endometrial biopsy at predicting live birth in the SAME women? That is a costly, concrete, falsifiable programme, not a shrug. DISAMBIGUATION BUILT INTO THE NO BRANCH, worth preregistering: a bare NO is confounded by menstruation — the functionalis you biopsied pre-conception is shed by design, so "no clonal continuity" could mean recruitment OR could mean you sampled cells that were destined to be shed while their relatives in the basalis were retained. The contemporaneous blood comparison resolves this asymmetrically: a POSITIVE match of decidual clones to contemporaneous blood establishes recruitment regardless of the shedding confound. So the NO branch must be scored as "decidua matches blood," not merely "decidua fails to match prior endometrium."
compartments_needed: Adjudication needs, from ONE woman, at TWO separated timepoints: A. PRE-CONCEPTION ENDOMETRIUM (functionalis, mid-luteal / window of implantation) — the putative source pool. B. PERIPHERAL BLOOD AT THE SAME PRE-CONCEPTION TIMEPOINT — not optional. This is the null against which any A-to-C clone sharing must be scored; without it, shared ancestry is uninterpretable because every NK cell in the woman shares an HSPC ancestor. C. DECIDUA FROM THE SUBSEQUENT PREGNANCY (first-trimester decidua basalis preferred; term decidua/basal plate as the feasible substitute) — the putative product pool. D. PERIPHERAL BLOOD CONTEMPORANEOUS WITH C — required to score the recruitment model positively rather than inferring it from a failed match to A (see the shedding confound in action_if_no). Needed additionally only on the NO branch, all obtainable at the same surgical event as C: E. DECIDUA PARIETALIS and ADJACENT NON-DECIDUALIZED ENDOMETRIUM. F. DECIDUA-RESIDENT CD34+/stage-3 NK PRECURSORS (Vacca 2011, PMID 21248224). Needed to root the clone tree (i.e. to convert "share an ancestor" into "how recently"), and essentially never available: G. BONE MARROW / HSPC compartment from the same woman. Needed only if one insists on testing the shedding-reservoir hypothesis directly: H. BASALIS / deep endometrium — see compartment_notes; this one is structurally unobtainable in the required pairing.
compartments_obtainable: PARTIAL — obtainable in the feasible pairing, low-yield in the fully-specified pairing, and one required compartment is structurally impossible. A (pre-conception endometrium): YES, easily. Outpatient Pipelle biopsy, no anaesthetic, already routine in recurrent-miscarriage / recurrent-implantation-failure clinics where uNK is quantified as standard (PMID 36592442, PMID 25150956, PMID 38164429). Repeatable across cycles. NON-INVASIVE SERIAL ALTERNATIVE EXISTS AND IS VALIDATED: menstrual effluent yields uterine NK whose KIR repertoire is "markedly different from those in peripheral blood NK cells," sampled paired with peripheral blood in the same women (PMID 27271316). This is the single biggest feasibility advantage S2 has over the other pregnancy-gated rows in this screen — it gives serial within-woman pre-conception sampling of the source compartment without a procedure. B and D (blood at both timepoints): YES, trivially. Venipuncture. C (decidua from the SAME woman's subsequent pregnancy): THIS IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, and it is doubly gated — ONLY DURING PREGNANCY and ONLY AT SURGERY. First/second-trimester decidua exists only via elective termination or miscarriage; term decidua only at caesarean or delivery. So the fully-specified design requires a woman who (i) consented to a pre-conception research sample, (ii) then conceived, and (iii) then terminated or miscarried that pregnancy. You cannot plan this, only enrich for it — recruiting in recurrent-miscarriage clinics raises the conversion rate because the subsequent-loss base rate is high and those women are already being biopsied. ASCERTAINMENT BIAS TO PREREGISTER: the first-trimester decidua you can actually obtain in a paired design comes disproportionately from losses, which is precisely the population whose uNK biology is hypothesised to be abnormal. THE FEASIBLE SUBSTITUTE: pre-conception endometrium (or serial menstrual effluent) paired with TERM decidua at elective caesarean is fully obtainable, single-timepoint, and unbiased by loss. Its cost is that at term the three-subset structure collapses anyway (Whettlock's term uNK form ONE cluster analysed alone, three only after integration), so the term design can answer pool-level carriage and nothing about subset structure — which is exactly the scope B1 says is decidable, so this is an acceptable trade. E and F: YES, same surgical event as C, no extra access cost. F is at the edge of feasibility on cell number (Vacca sorted only hundreds of decidual CD34+ cells per well). G (bone marrow, to root the tree): NO. Not obtainable from termination or caesarean donors; a marrow aspirate is never taken alongside either. So "how recently" must be estimated from clone-size structure and the blood baseline rather than from a rooted phylogeny. H (basalis / deep endometrium): STRUCTURALLY UNOBTAINABLE IN THE REQUIRED PAIRING. The basalis requires hysterectomy or a deceased donor — Garcia-Alonso 2021 (PMID 34857954) used 6 deceased-donor whole uteri for exactly this reason. Hysterectomy ends fertility, so NO WOMAN CAN SUPPLY BOTH HER BASALIS AND HER LATER DECIDUA. This is a permanent hole, and it sits under the strongest confound in the design (functionalis shedding), which is why the menstrual-effluent serial census in action_if_yes is the workaround rather than a luxury. THE ONE HUMAN SETTING WHERE THE PRIMITIVE IS FREE AND THE PAIRING ALREADY EXISTS: uterus-transplant recipients. Donor-vs-recipient SNP and HLA disparity supplies a permanent, cell-intrinsic lineage label with no barcoding and no mtDNA power problem, and these women are serially biopsied before pregnancy and then deliver by caesarean, so A and C come from one woman by construction. Strunz 2026 (PMID 41811987) has already run the SNP demultiplex on non-pregnant endometrium in this cohort; Asiimwe 2026 (PMID 41811989) is the same cohort. THREE CAVEATS: n is very small (uterus transplant is rare, and rarer still with a live birth); recipients are on tacrolimus, which Strunz 2026 itself shows inhibits NFAT and "affected de novo induction of tissue-residency features in vitro," so the residency biology under test is pharmacologically perturbed; and donor/recipient is a TWO-BIN label, not a clone-level one — it answers "was the pool replaced from circulation" but returns no clone-level recency and no subset-resolved structure.
nearest_occupant: NEAREST OCCUPANT — Asiimwe R, Knott B, Greene ME, ... Porrett PM. "Inhibition of NFAT after human uterus transplant promotes loss of tissue-resident NK cells and attendant pregnancy complications." Sci Transl Med 2026;18(840):eadp2196. PMID 41811989, PMC13095030. What they did (read from PMC full text, not the abstract): 5 uterus-transplant (UTx) donor:recipient pairs. Donor and recipient genotypes established by whole-exome sequencing of donor and recipient PBMCs for 4 of the 5 pairs. Endometrial biopsies collected pre-pregnancy (>30 days post-transplant) at multiple timepoints AND decidua collected at cesarean delivery FROM THE SAME PATIENTS. scRNA-seq, flow, IF. How it differs — and this is the sharp point. They ran donor-vs-recipient origin assignment on the ENDOMETRIUM only (Fig 2C-D; recipient-derived cells predominate). They did NOT carry the genotype assignment into the DECIDUA. Decidual samples were analyzed for composition and transcriptional state only. No TCR, no mtDNA, no barcode anywhere in the paper. So the exact two-timepoint paired human compartment set that claim S2 requires (compartments A and C, same woman, pre-conception then pregnancy) has ALREADY BEEN COLLECTED, with WES genotypes already in hand, and the origin analysis was performed on A and then not performed on C. The claim is unoccupied by one analysis on an existing cohort. Note the axis they can read is a coarse binary graft-vs-recipient marker under immunosuppression, not clonal ancestry, and tacrolimus in this cohort itself depletes tissue-resident uNK — so even the extended analysis would answer "graft-resident vs recipient-circulation," not "which uNK clones became which dNK clones," and would do so in a pharmacologically distorted uterus. SECOND OCCUPANT — Strunz B, Ivarsson MA, ... Björkström NK. "Reconstitution of the uterine immune milieu after uterus or hematopoietic stem cell transplantation." Sci Transl Med 2026;18(840):eadp2583. PMID 41811987. Single-cell SNP-based donor/recipient demultiplexing plus HLA-disparity flow, in UTx and HSCT recipients. Recipient-derived immune cells replaced donor immune cells after UTx; HSCT gave near-complete donor-derived reconstitution including tissue-resident lymphocytes; in one patient male-origin cells reconstituted the endometrium after HSCT (an XY lineage marker). ENDOMETRIUM ONLY, non-pregnant, no decidua, no clonal barcode. Its predecessor, Strunz B et al., Sci Immunol 2021;6:eabb7800 (PMID 33617461), used human uterus transplantation and monozygotic twins to show uNK carry the recipient genotype, i.e. the uNK niche is replenished from circulation. That result is directly load-bearing against the S2 framing: if the endometrial uNK pool is itself continuously blood-replenished on a months timescale, ongoing common blood input becomes an alternative explanation for any A-to-C clone sharing, on top of the shared-HSPC-ancestor null the claim already budgets for in compartments B and D. THIRD OCCUPANT (mouse, same structural question, non-clonal tool, and the field disagrees with itself) — Sojka DK, ... Yokoyama WM. J Immunol 2018;201:2551 (PMID 30275046): NKp46 reporter mouse + parabiosis + induced deciduoma; uNK accumulating during decidualization were locally PROLIFERATING pre-existing trNK, migrating NK contributed nothing. Directly contradicted by the same first author seven years later: Tatematsu BK, Sojka DK. Mucosal Immunol 2025;18:390 (PMID 39708955): parabiosis + intravascular labeling; progesterone-responsive uterine trNK are DERIVED FROM PERIPHERAL cNK. Also Chiossone L, Vacca P, ... Mingari MC. Haematologica 2014;99:448 (PMID 24179150): adoptive transfer of CD34+ progenitors generating dNK in situ. And a T-bet fate map, Rosa26-RFP x Tbx21-Cre across virgin uterus/decidua/placenta through gestation (PMID 41782473, 2026) — a marker-history Cre fate map, which records "ever expressed T-bet," not shared ancestry between two cells. None of these is a clonal barcode; parabiosis reads migration/residency, Cre fate mapping reads marker history. The mouse structural analogue is occupied by lineage-adjacent tools and is currently answered two contradictory ways. crossfield_occupancy: YES — heavily occupied in the T cell and myeloid fields, partially in NK/ILC. The structural question S2 asks ("is a tissue-resident pool the clonal descendant of a pre-existing local pool, or of ongoing input from circulation?") has been answered with real clonal tools elsewhere. This is a borrowed-mechanism claim and the occupancy lives in the fields it was borrowed from. T CELL FIELD — answered, using TCR as the endogenous clonal barcode. Poon MML, ... Farber DL. "Tissue adaptation and clonal segregation of human memory T cells in barrier sites." Nat Immunol 2023;24:309 (PMID 36658238) — blood plus multiple tissues from the same organ donor, clonal segregation between tissue and blood established directly. Extended by cross-tissue intra-donor clonal mapping across the gut-liver-blood axis (PMID 41615802, 2026), blood-vs-tonsil compartmentalized clones and phenotypic trajectories (PMID 41308653, 2025), and repertoire maintenance by subset and tissue site (PMID 34127056). Notably it is occupied IN DECIDUA specifically: clonally expanded decidual effector Tregs scored against blood by TCR in normal pregnancy vs preeclampsia (PMID 30197648, 2018). So the decidua-vs-blood clonal-continuity question has already been asked and answered for T cells at the same interface — with a barcode NK cells do not have, which is precisely why the NK version is still open. MYELOID FIELD — answered, and with the exact tool class proposed for S2. Belk JA, ... Weissman IL, Chang HY, Jaiswal S. "Somatic mutations reveal the ontogeny of human microglia." bioRxiv 2026 (PMID 42239322, PMC13228375): accumulated somatic mutations as per-clone labels plus single-cell mtDNA-variant lineage tracing across 20 aged humans, to decide whether a resident tissue pool is self-maintained or replenished by marrow-derived influx. Answer: widespread influx, sometimes a large fraction of the pool. That is structurally the same adjudication S2 wants, executed in brain, on post-mortem tissue, with the mtDNA primitive. Precedent for feasibility of the method; also a warning that the answer in other tissues has come back "influx," matching what the human uterus-transplant chimerism data already suggest. NK / ILC FIELD — partially occupied, and the gap is named. Dunbar lab barcoded macaque HSPC transplant resolved tissue-NK vs blood-NK clonal relationships across liver, spleen, lung, GI (PMID 36605190) — finding tissue-specific TR-NK clones and shared liver/spleen clone sets — and explicitly flagged decidual NK as the compartment not yet examined at a clonal level. Adjacent NK clonal work exists: clonal + single-cell analysis separating human NK from noncytotoxic ILCs on a temporal developmental map (PMID 38484189, Blood Adv 2024); barcode-based clonal expansion and epigenetic inheritance of long-lasting NK memory in mouse MCMV (PMID 36289449, Nat Immunol 2022); CMV effects on macaque NK clonal repertoire (PMID 31649681); barcoded CAR-NK delivery in macaque/human NK (PMID 40621477). ILC ontogeny has layered-wave fate mapping (PMID 32783932). So the NK field has the barcode machinery and has pointed it at every tissue except this one.

why: TRUE, but only for the ancestry half of the claim — which is also the load-bearing half. S3 decomposes into two propositions that the evidence base conflates. (a) ANCESTRY: the dNK of a pregnancy are the progeny of the uterine NK resident in that same uterus before conception. This is the canonical "the progeny of A are B" form and is exactly what the clonal primitive delivers. (b) CONVERSION/FUNCTION: eNK are "special immature cells that await pregnancy" that acquire dNK function under IL-15 (Manaster 2008 PMID 18641324 — the INF_INVITRO source that sets Phase A's strongest class). (b) is the "A becomes functionally B-like" form and is NOT decidable by lineage: barcoding cannot say a cell acquired KIR-mediated licensing, IFN-g/VEGF output, or spiral-artery-remodelling capacity. A positive lineage answer licenses (a) only and must not be read as confirming (b). The row passes B1 because the downstream dependency (pre-conception uNK biopsy testing) rests on (a), not (b). It escapes the reversible-state trap because the two live rival hypotheses predict DIFFERENT clonal structures, not the same one. Local persistence/expansion predicts dNK clone families enriched for families already resident in that woman's pre-conception endometrium, above what her contemporaneous circulating NK pool would supply. Recruitment/de novo generation (supported by Chantakru 2002 uterine grafts PMID 11751942, Chiossone 2014 PMID 24179150, Strunz 2026 STM chimerism after uterus/HSC transplant PMID 41811987, and by monthly shedding of the functionalis) predicts dNK clones drawn from the contemporaneous circulating spectrum with no uterus-specific enrichment. These differ in "how recently do these two cells share an ancestor", so the primitive discriminates. Two caveats that are design requirements, not decidability failures. (i) The naive test is degenerate — every hematopoietic cell in one woman shares an ancestor — so the question must be posed as an ENRICHMENT test of pre-conception endometrial clone families in the pregnancy dNK pool against a contemporaneous autologous blood-NK reference, never as a bare shared-ancestor test. (ii) The pre-conception sample must come from the conception cycle, or be explicitly calibrated against measured cycle-to-cycle turnover, because the functionalis and most of its uNK are shed at every menstruation; a NO from a sample taken cycles earlier is uninformative about the cycle-to-pregnancy transition specifically, since those clones would have been lost to menstruation regardless of pregnancy.
action_if_yes: YES = dNK clone families are significantly enriched for clones resident in that woman's pre-conception endometrium, above her contemporaneous blood-NK baseline. Next experiment: the pre-conception uterine CLONE becomes the unit of prediction, so run a prospective clone-tracked outcome study in the population where the claim is load-bearing — recurrent-miscarriage / recurrent-implantation-failure clinics, which already take luteal-phase endometrial biopsies and already sell CD56+ uNK density as a triage test (PMID 35265977). Bank the conception-cycle pre-conception sample (menstrual-cup MNC and/or Pipelle biopsy), then genotype the ensuing pregnancy's decidua (products of conception at miscarriage, or decidua basalis at delivery) and ask: (1) WHICH pre-conception clones expand — is pregnancy a uniform expansion of the resident pool or a selective sweep of a minority of clones, which are opposite biological pictures both compatible with a bare YES; (2) whether a pre-conception CLONAL parameter (clone-size distribution, oligoclonality, the KIR/education phenotype carried by persisting clones) predicts outcome better than the density number currently sold, i.e. re-base the existing test on the clone rather than the cell count. Second, distinct experiment enabled only by YES: test the Gamliel 2018 PTdNK "trained memory" claim (PMID 29768178) at clone level — decidua from pregnancy 1 and pregnancy 2 in the same woman, asking whether the NKG2C-hi/LILRB1-hi PTdNK of the second pregnancy are literally surviving clones of the first. That is the only version of the memory claim lineage can adjudicate, and it is incoherent under NO.
action_if_no: NO = dNK clone families are drawn from the contemporaneous circulating spectrum with no enrichment for that woman's pre-conception endometrial clones — the compartment is refilled, not carried over. Next experiment: the target compartment moves out of the uterus. (1) SOURCE ASSIGNMENT — paired within-pregnancy mtscATAC of decidua plus peripheral blood NK subsets plus circulating CD34+/CD56-bright precursors from the same woman, to assign the dNK founder clones to a specific circulating population rather than merely excluding the endometrium. This is a positive assignment, not a restatement of the negative. (2) TIMING — serial blood sampling across the peri-implantation window and early gestation to date when the founder clones leave the circulation. That defines the intervention window and cannot be recovered from the paired endpoint alone. (3) CLINICAL — a NO removes the lineage premise from pre-conception uNK biopsy testing, because the biopsy would be measuring a population that no longer exists by the time the outcome it predicts occurs. The actionable follow-up is a head-to-head predictive study: does a peri-conception BLOOD NK clonal/subset measure predict pregnancy outcome as well as or better than luteal-phase endometrial CD56+ density? A positive result replaces an invasive commercial test with a blood test; a negative result retires the biomarker rather than relocating it. Compartment sampled, sampling schedule, and clinical decision all change relative to YES.
compartments_needed: Three, of which the blood reference is mandatory rather than optional. A. Uterine/endometrial NK from the NON-PREGNANT cycling uterus of woman W, luteal/secretory phase, ideally of the conception cycle itself. Route: Pipelle/aspiration biopsy, or menstrual-cup mononuclear cells. B. Decidual NK from the SAME woman W in her subsequent pregnancy: first-trimester decidua (6-15 wk, the canonical dNK compartment), or failing that decidua basalis at delivery. C. Contemporaneous autologous peripheral blood NK at BOTH timepoints — the reference against which endometrium-specific clonal enrichment is measured. Without C the comparison is degenerate, because all of W's hematopoietic cells share ancestry and the test returns a trivial YES. Desirable additions: serial menstrual-cup samples across consecutive non-conception cycles in the same woman, to calibrate baseline cycle-to-cycle clonal turnover from menstrual shedding; circulating CD34+/CD56-bright precursors for the NO-branch source assignment. Bone marrow would help but is not routinely obtainable in this population — drop it.
compartments_obtainable: PARTIAL. Same individual: YES, but only longitudinally, prospectively, and with banking. Simultaneously: NO — and that is a logical impossibility rather than a logistics problem, since one uterus cannot be non-pregnant and decidualized at the same instant. A and B are necessarily separated by months to years. Zero paired human samples exist in the located literature, and not for want of trying. The Phase A primary source says so outright (Feyaerts 2024 PMID 38571943: "we had no access to paired samples, i.e. endometrial and decidual NK cells from the same individual ... this poses inconceivable logistic and ethical barriers"), and I independently confirmed a second 2024 study repeating the identical unpaired architecture (Front Immunol 10.3389/fimmu.2024.1364036, Methods checked: n=4 non-pregnant endometrial biopsies vs n=4 DIFFERENT women's elective-termination first-trimester tissue). Per compartment: A is easy — outpatient, non-surgical, repeatable, already routine in exactly the RM/RIF population where the claim is load-bearing; the menstrual-cup route is fully non-invasive and reproducible between women and cycles (PMID 24249743), though it remains an unvalidated proxy for biopsy in the same woman. C is trivial at both timepoints. B is the binding constraint: PREGNANCY-ONLY by definition and procedure-tethered — first-trimester decidua only at elective termination or from products of conception after miscarriage; term decidua basalis only at delivery/Caesarean. B is NOT post-mortem-only, NOT mouse-only, and needs no procedure that would not otherwise occur. Three feasible pairing routes, with their costs. (1) RM/RIF prospective cohort — bank the luteal biopsy already being taken, capture first-trimester decidua from women who conceive and miscarry. Gives the canonical compartment, but the paired cohort is selected for pregnancy failure and may not represent normal pregnancy, which matters because recruitment-vs-persistence could itself differ in failing pregnancies. (2) Unselected cohort followed to delivery — high pairing yield, but the pregnancy compartment is term decidua, by which time uNK have declined and may not be the first-trimester dNK the claim is about. why: DECIDABLE, but only in the same-lineage/different-lineage form, and only with the label applied downstream of the NK progenitor. WHY TRUE. The falsifiable content Phase A itself names — conversion vs "two independent lineages" — is exactly an MRCA-depth question, which is what the primitive returns. Under two independent lineages, mature blood cNK and liver/skin trNK coalesce only at or above the common progenitor: every cross-compartment cell pair has a deep MRCA, while within-compartment pairs can be shallow. Under conversion, individual clones straddle the two compartments with shallow, post-progenitor MRCAs. That asymmetry in the cross- vs within-compartment coalescent-depth distribution is a direct readout of "do they share an ancestor and how recently," so the claim's load-bearing alternative is adjudicable. WHAT IS NOT DECIDABLE, AND MUST BE SCOPED OUT. (1) Direction. A clone found in both compartments is equally consistent with cNK -> trNK, with trNK export back to blood, and with a shared recent precursor that seeded both in parallel. The arrow in "cNK -> trNK" is NOT recovered by clonal structure alone; it needs a timestamp (label the mature cNK pool only, after the trNK pool already exists) so that appearance of label in trNK is directional by construction. (2) The parenthetical, "acquisition of a residency phenotype," read literally as a phenotype/state statement, is NOT decidable — lineage does not measure whether residency was acquired, only whether the cells are clonally continuous. (3) The reversible-state trap partially bites. If residency is reversible (an ex-trNK can re-enter circulation, as documented for ex-TRM in the T-cell field), shared clones cannot separate one-way conversion from a single interconverting pool — both give clones spanning both compartments. Crucially, though, the reversibility ambiguity sits INSIDE the "one lineage" branch; it does not collapse the one-lineage vs two-lineage discrimination, which is why this is TRUE rather than FALSE. DESIGN CONSTRAINT THAT FALLS OUT OF THE PRIMITIVE. HSC/HSPC-level barcoding cannot decide this claim: both hypotheses predict shared HSPC barcodes across compartments, because both candidate lineages descend from the same HSCs. This is exactly the ceiling on Wu 2022 (PMID 36605190 / PMC9808525, barcoded autologous HSPC transplant in rhesus, blood vs liver/spleen/lung/GI NK) — they observe both PB-shared and tissue-private NK clones, but at HSPC-clone resolution "shared" does not separate "a cNK converted" from "one HSPC clone independently fed two lineages." The decidable design needs either an inducible label at or below the mature cNK stage (Ncr1-CreERT2 x barcode/Confetti, induced after the resident pool is established) or enough sub-clonal resolution (mtDNA sub-clone structure via mtscATAC-seq/MAESTER, rooted on same-donor HSPCs) to measure coalescent DEPTH rather than mere set overlap.
action_if_yes: YES = clones straddle mature circulating cNK and tissue trNK with shallow (post-progenitor) MRCA; the trNK pool is clonally continuous with the mature circulating pool. Very next experiment: the conversion flux is now a measurable quantity, so perturb the source and re-read the SAME clonal output. Concretely — Ncr1-CreERT2 driving both the inducible barcode/Confetti and Tgfbr2-flox (TGF-betaRII is the named requirement in the sibling uterine claim, Barahona/Yokoyama), tamoxifen after the resident pool is established, then score whether cNK-derived barcodes still enter the liver/skin trNK compartment and at what rate. Paired arm: naive vs locally infected tissue (VACV/HSV ear skin, per the Gasteiger-lab design, PMID 38157853) to test whether entry is a steady-state trickle or inflammation-gated — which is the specific thing Sojka parabiosis could not see, since parabiosis tests pool replenishment at steady state, not inducible entry. This is a new mouse, a new perturbation, and a new statistic (barcode entry rate under a genetic block). It is motivated ONLY by YES: with NO there is no source to knock out.
action_if_no: NO = cross-compartment MRCAs are uniformly deep; trNK clones are tissue-private and coalesce with blood cNK only at or above the progenitor. Very next experiment: the question flips from "how much flux" to "which progenitor, and when," which is a different sampling program, not a conclusion. Concretely — move the labeling window earlier and swap in the candidate source compartments: pulse-label in the fetal/perinatal window, and compare an ILC-progenitor-restricted CreER (Il7r/Rag1/PLZF-class) against Ncr1-CreER, asking which progenitor compartment shares a SHALLOW MRCA with adult liver trNK. In parallel, use the within-tissue clone-size distribution to test whether the resident pool is self-maintained by local proliferation rather than fed from outside at all. In the human arm this means dropping blood cNK as the comparator and adding fetal liver / BM ILC progenitors / adult BM CD34+ to the panel. Precedent that this branch is productive rather than terminal: the tissue-macrophage field's NO answer (tissue macrophages are not monocyte-derived) is what launched the fetal-origin program. Same structural shape here.
compartments_needed: THREE compartments, needed simultaneously from one individual: A. Circulating conventional NK — peripheral blood (human venipuncture; mouse blood + spleen). Trivial. B. Tissue-resident NK from ONE defined tissue. The claim must name the tissue, because feasibility differs sharply: - LIVER (the compartment Sojka 2014 parabiosis actually addresses): human via deceased-donor liver perfusate, or via surgical resection (hepatectomy/metastasectomy), both with paired blood from the same individual. - SKIN: punch biopsy + paired blood, outpatient and repeatable — but trNK are rare in normal human skin, so cell-number limiting. - UTERUS/ENDOMETRIUM: pipelle biopsy + paired blood, outpatient, repeatable, non-pregnant; uNK are abundant, which is the best cell-number profile of the options. Decidua proper is pregnancy-only (termination/delivery). - LUNG/GUT: resection or endoscopic biopsy + paired blood. C. A ROOTING compartment: HSPC/progenitors (BM aspirate or mobilised CD34+) from the SAME individual. This is not optional. Without it you cannot convert "clone shared vs private" into "MRCA shallow vs deep," and the whole discrimination in B1 collapses — you cannot distinguish a shared HSPC clone from a genuine peripheral conversion.
compartments_obtainable: TRUE, with a cell-number caveat that is the real bottleneck. Paired A+B from one living human is routine: blood + endometrial pipelle (outpatient), blood + skin punch, blood + liver resection at surgery. None of the required compartments is post-mortem-only, pregnancy-only, or mouse-only. Adding C from a living donor costs one extra invasive procedure (BM aspirate). All three come paired and unforced from a single deceased organ donor (vertebral-body BM + blood + multiple solid organs), which is the standard organ-donor tissue pipeline. Verified precedent that in-life paired sampling works in a primate: Wu 2022 (PMID 36605190) took liver and spleen by laparoscopy, gut by endoscopic pinch biopsy, and LN by surgical excision, serially, from LIVING barcoded macaques alongside blood. THE CAVEAT, from the same paper: subset-resolved sorting of tissue NK (CD56/CD16 subsets out of each organ) was only possible in the ONE animal that came to autopsy — the serial in-life biopsies gave paired tissue+blood but not enough cells to sort resident NK subsets. So paired sampling is obtainable; paired sampling at the DEPTH needed for clonal statistics on a rare resident subset pushes you toward organ-donor, autopsy, or surgical-resection-scale material rather than needle biopsy. This is the practical constraint that should be preregistered, and it argues for endometrium (abundant uNK, repeatable outpatient sampling) or resection-scale liver over skin.
nearest_occupant: Two co-nearest occupants, one per axis. NEAREST ON THE CLONAL PRIMITIVE: Wu et al. 2022, PMID 36605190 (Front Immunol, PMC9808525). It uses exactly the primitive in question (shared-ancestor barcodes), in a large outbred primate, with paired blood + liver + spleen + lung + GI from the same animal, AND with the HSPC rooting compartment supplied by construction. HOW IT DIFFERS: (a) not human, and requires myeloablative TBI + autologous transplant, so every clonal structure it reports is post-transplant reconstitution, not steady-state adult homeostasis; (b) it stratifies NK by CD56/CD16 only — it never gates on the canonical residency markers (CD69, CD49a, CD103, CXCR6) that define the "residency phenotype" the claim is about, so its "TR NK" is operationally "NK recovered from a tissue," which is a weaker definition than the claim uses; (c) because the barcode is installed in the HSPC, a shared barcode between blood NK and tissue NK proves a shared HSPC ancestor, NOT that a mature circulating cNK converted in the periphery — it therefore cannot by itself separate "parallel HSPC output to two sites" from "peripheral conversion," which is the exact discrimination B1 needs; (d) n is small (a handful of animals) and the paper itself reports the trNK clonal pattern was "more heterogeneous between individual animals." NEAREST IN HUMAN: Liu et al., Cancer Cell 2026, PMID 42242233 (preprint 40777278). Human, mtDNA clonal, matched blood + non-involved tissue + tumor in one individual, NK included, and it already reports the two possible answers coexisting (blood NK clones found in tissue; tumor NK clones absent from blood). HOW IT DIFFERS: (a) NK are a side observation, not the paper's object — the analysis and the headline are monocyte-to-macrophage/DC3; (b) cell types are annotated from chromatin accessibility (NCR1, GNLY, KLRD1) into a merged "NK/ILC" cluster, with NO residency-marker stratification, so it never separates cNK from trNK — it separates blood-NK from tissue-NK by sampling site, which is the confound, not the answer; (c) tissue is lung (NILT and tumor) and ovarian tumor — not liver, not endometrium, not normal skin; every donor is a cancer patient, several treatment-exposed; (d) no BM/HSPC rooting compartment at all, so MRCA depth is inferred only from mtDNA variant sharing depth; (e) NK numbers are thin — they state NK are depleted in tumor relative to NILT and "rarely detected in most tumors," with the oligoclonal NK finding resting on a single donor (SU-O-005) and the blood-enriched NK clones on a single donor (SU-L-005). RESIDUAL UNOCCUPIED SLICE, stated precisely so it is not overclaimed: human, non-malignant tissue, NK explicitly stratified by CD69/CD49a/CXCR6 residency phenotype, with a paired BM/HSPC rooting compartment. That is narrow, and both flanking papers would likely be read by reviewers as having already settled the direction.
crossfield_occupancy: G4 applies squarely — "acquisition of tissue residency" is a borrowed mechanism, and the field it was borrowed from has already answered the identical structural question with clonal tools, in humans, at larger n. why: The fork T3 actually turns on is invisible to a shared-ancestor primitive. Three reasons, in order of force. (1) THE CONTESTED DISTINCTION IS A MATURATION STAGE INSIDE ONE CLONAL BRANCH, NOT A BRANCH POINT. T3 asserts that a MATURE circulating CD16+ pbNK enters decidua and converts. Its live competitor after the Phase A audit is not "decidual NK are non-haematopoietic" - it is that a BLOOD-BORNE IMMATURE PRECURSOR (CD34+ or CD34-CD117+CD94- stage-3) crosses into the uterus and matures locally (Chantakru 2002 PMID 11751942; Male 2010 PMID 20802153; Vacca 2011 PMID 21248224; Strunz 2021 PMID 33617461). A mature pbNK and its sibling precursor are on the SAME clonal branch and carry the SAME mark, because the mark is fixed upstream of both. Clone membership is stage-agnostic and undirected: it says "these two cells share an ancestor", never "which one was the immigrant" or "what state it was in when it crossed the endothelium". Both hypotheses therefore predict the identical clonal structure - the prompt's own disqualifying condition. (2) THE DEPTH RESOLUTION IS WRONG BY ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE, and this is documented, not speculative. Rueckert 2022 Nat Immunol PMID 36289449, the one study that has actually run mtscATAC/mgatk on human NK cells, states in its own results that for CONVENTIONAL (non-adaptive, non-expanded) NK cells the mitochondrial mutations "do not flag clonal expansions but might instead be present already on the progenitor level". Wang 2025 Genome Biol PMID 40134031 goes further: the majority of purported clone-informative variants are PRE-EXISTING heteroplasmies present in the first cell, not de novo marks acquired during recent divisions. So the "how recently" that mtDNA delivers dates the common ancestor to an embryonic/HSC-level node, far above the pbNK-vs-precursor node T3 depends on. Every maternal haematopoietic cell in that woman - blood NK, decidual NK, decidual CD34+, and a uterus-resident precursor seeded years earlier - passes the shared-ancestor test. (3) THE ENDPOINT IS A REVERSIBLE, ENVIRONMENT-IMPOSED STATE, NOT A LINEAGE DESTINATION. "dNK-like" is operationally CD16-lo/CD9+/CD49a+/CD103+/KIR+, a TGF-beta-driven residency imprint that Keskin's own Discussion concedes "may not be specific to the decidual tissue but may occur when NK cells enter any tissue expressing TGF-beta", and that Cerdeira 2013 Fig 1 shows RUNNING BACKWARDS - ex vivo dNK lose KIR and regain cytotoxicity within 7-10 days of culture (registry claim R3 is exactly this reversal). An NK cell sitting in decidua is dNK-like whatever its recent ancestry, and an NK cell in blood is not, whatever its ancestry. Ancestry neither determines nor reports the state. NOTE ON WHAT IS DECIDABLE: a coarser question - "is the human uterine NK pool filled from the circulation at all?" - is a genuine ancestry question, but it is not T3, and it has already been answered in vivo in humans by donor/recipient genotyping rather than by barcoding (Strunz 2021 PMID 33617461, uNK carry recipient genotype after uterus transplant; Strunz 2026 Sci Transl Med PMID 41811987, donor-derived endometrial tissue-resident lymphocytes after HSCT, one case male-origin; both recorded abstract-level only in Phase A). G4 note: the structurally identical question in the T cell field - are tissue-resident cells clonally continuous with blood? - is routinely settled with TCR clonotype, a true per-cell somatic barcode with resolution mtDNA does not approach (e.g. PMID 41615802, intra-donor cross-tissue T cell clonal mapping across gut-liver-blood). NK cells have no rearranged receptor, which is precisely why the NK field is reaching for mtDNA and precisely why it cannot reach the depth this claim needs.

THE VERY NEXT EXPERIMENT: you would have to determine whether the cell that crossed into the decidua was a mature CD16+ pbNK (T3 as stated) or a blood-borne CD34+/CD117+ stage-3 precursor that matured in situ. NO LINEAGE EXPERIMENT CAN DO THIS - the two candidates share a branch and share the mark - so the follow-up is not a barcoding experiment at all. It is a stage-resolved in vivo tracking tool that does not exist for humans: there is no human equivalent of the i.v. anti-CD45 intravascular-exclusion label or the Ncr1-iCre stage-restricted fate map that Barahona/Yokoyama used in mouse (eLife 2026 PMID 42417504, which is registry claim T2, not T3). So the YES branch terminates in the sentence "the uterine NK niche is filled from the circulation, and we move on" - which is (a) already reported in vivo in humans by transplant-chimerism genotyping (Strunz PMID 33617461; PMID 41811987), and (b) leaves T3's entire distinctive content, MATURE pbNK plus TGF-beta-driven conversion, exactly where the Phase A audit left it. This branch is vacuous. It is also the near-certain outcome: every dNK variant of the kind mtDNA detects is a pre-existing/progenitor-level heteroplasmy that is by construction also present in that woman's blood (PMID 40134031; PMID 36289449), AND maternal blood contamination of an enzymatically digested decidua manufactures the identical result. The branch that carries no information is the branch you will almost certainly get, and it is indistinguishable from the assay's dominant artefact.
action_if_no: Same adjudicating run. compartments_needed: Five, in descending order of necessity. compartments_obtainable: PARTIAL - and it fails on exactly the compartments the fork needs. (A)+(B) PAIRED FROM ONE WOMAN: YES, routinely, and this is genuinely T3's strongest feature relative to other rows in this registry. First-trimester elective termination (6-12 wk) yields decidua with a same-visit venous draw; at term, PMID 41808348 (2026) collected placenta, decidua and matched maternal blood from the same donors at scheduled caesarean and sorted NK from mBlood/DPI/decidua of 6 MATCHED donors, so the pairing is demonstrated, not hypothetical. (D) NON-PREGNANT ENDOMETRIUM FROM THE SAME WOMAN: NOT obtainable simultaneously. Pre-pregnancy endometrium and pregnancy decidua from one individual requires prospective longitudinal recruitment - biopsy, then conception, then termination or delivery - which is a study design, not a sample request, and exists in no archived dataset. (E) BONE MARROW: not obtainable from termination or caesarean donors. The clone tree cannot be rooted, so "how recently" is unmeasurable in the very individuals who supply A and B. TIMING AND ACCESS CONSTRAINTS, EXPLICIT: compartment B exists ONLY DURING PREGNANCY and ONLY at surgery (termination or caesarean); sampling is destructive and single-timepoint, so the same woman's decidua can never be resampled before/after; compartment D needs a separate procedure at a separate time.

why: The claim decomposes into three parts, and the part that carries the claim is not the part barcoding can see. (1) "Glycodelin-A DRIVES" is molecular attribution. The primitive returns whether two cells share an ancestor and how recently; it is blind to WHICH signal produced a state. A perfect clonal read showing blood NK gave rise to the CD9+CD49a+ cells would not name GdA as the cause, and a perfect clonal read showing no relationship would not exclude GdA from acting on whatever precursor does make dNK. (2) "dNK-LIKE PHENOTYPE" is a marker state, not an ancestry relation - lineage does not measure phenotype causation. (3) The one structurally clean question here - is the day-5 CD9+CD49a+ output the progeny of CD9-CD49a- day-0 cells (conversion), or the expansion of a CD9+CD49a+ fraction present at day 0 (selection)? - IS decidable in principle, and it is exactly Phase A's strongest alternative explanation. But that is a narrow within-culture ancestry question, not the claim as written, and it still cannot license the verb "drives". Decisively, this is the preregistered REVERSIBLE-STATE case. CD56bright/CD9/CD49a residency markers are a reversible state inside one NK lineage, not a lineage bifurcation: Niehrs et al. Nat Immunol 2025 (PMID 41087727) show human CD56bright NK enter tissue transiently and egress via lymphatics to recirculate, and Orrantia et al. iScience 2022 (PMID 36262311) show CD9 and the decidual-like signature are acquired by ordinary blood NK during proliferation-dominated reconstitution in vivo. So clonal sharing between the "blood NK" and "dNK-like" marker compartments is produced equally by a conversion model, by a selection-then-reversion model, and by plain recirculation - and absence of sharing is equally consistent with GdA acting on the local decidual CD34+ precursor route (Vacca et al. PNAS 2011, PMID 21248224). Both answers are consistent with the same clonal structure, which is the definition of not decidable by this primitive.
action_if_yes: YES = the CD9+CD49a+VEGF+ "dNK-like" cells are clonal progeny of CD16-CD56bright blood NK (in vitro: barcode day-0 sorted CD9-CD49a- cells and recover barcodes in the day-5 CD9+ gate; in vivo: shared mtDNA/somatic-epimutation clonotypes between a woman's peripheral blood NK and her decidual NK). Very next experiment: a GdA specificity-and-necessity perturbation with the readout unchanged - GdA vs de-sialylated GdA vs an irrelevant sialylated glycoprotein at matched 5 ug/mL protein load (the load control Lee 2019 lacks), plus L-selectin blockade and PAEP knockdown in endometrial epithelial organoid conditioned medium, run head-to-head against the TGF-beta arm (Keskin 2007, PMID 17360654) and the hypoxia+TGF-beta1+decitabine arm (Cerdeira 2013, PMID 23487420) that already yield the same CD9+CD49a+VEGF+ output, scoring CD9/CD49a/CD151/CD158a/VEGF.
action_if_no: NO = no clonal relationship; the CD9+CD49a+ cells are a selected/expanded pre-existing fraction, or decidual NK are not recent progeny of circulating NK at all. Very next experiment: run the identical GdA perturbation on the compartment that does give rise to dNK - decidual CD34+ precursors differentiating on decidual stroma (Vacca 2011) - adding and withholding GdA with the same de-sialylated-GdA, load, and anti-L-selectin controls and the same CD9/CD49a/CD151/CD158a/VEGF panel. Same reagent, same controls, same readout, same success criterion; only the cell placed in the well changes.
compartments_needed: Minimum pair for adjudication: (A) peripheral blood NK, both CD16-CD56bright and CD56dim gates, from a pregnant woman; (B) decidual NK (CD9+CD49a+CD56superbright) from the SAME woman's decidua basalis/parietalis. Because the GdA exposure window is progesterone-driven and first-trimester-weighted, compartment B must be GdA-high first-trimester decidua, not term tissue, for the claim's own premise to hold. Strongly desirable additions: (C) pre-pregnancy secretory-phase endometrial uNK from the same woman in a prior cycle, to catch the endometrial-to-decidual step rather than only its endpoint; (D) the decidual CD34+ precursor compartment (Vacca 2011), which travels with B and is the competing origin that any clonal result must be scored against; (E) bone marrow, only if the question is pushed back to the HSC-level ancestor. For an in-vitro-only version, the "compartments" collapse to day-0 sorted CD9-CD49a- CD56bright NK and the day-5 CD9+CD49a+ population from one culture, which is trivially paired but answers only the narrow selection-vs-conversion sub-question.
compartments_obtainable: Partly, and only under a hard surgical-and-pregnancy constraint. A+B paired from one human: YES in principle and routinely done for phenotyping - it is exactly the sourcing Lee 2019 used - but first-trimester decidua is obtainable ONLY at surgery, specifically surgical termination of pregnancy, and ONLY during pregnancy; term decidua parietalis requires Caesarean section or delivery. That makes A+B a single terminal timepoint per woman with no repeat sampling and no before/after GdA-exposure comparison in the same individual, which is fatal for a claim about a factor driving a transition over time. Not post-mortem-restricted. C is separately obtainable as an outpatient Pipelle endometrial biopsy in a prior cycle, so a preconception cohort could in principle assemble blood + endometrium longitudinally (cohorts of this scale exist - PMID 40561039 biopsied 924 women pre-pregnancy), but the terminal decidual sample still requires a pregnancy ending in surgery, so the full A+B+C set is only completable in women whose pregnancies are terminated or delivered surgically. D comes with B at no extra access cost. E (bone marrow) requires a separate aspirate essentially never taken alongside a termination, so an HSC-anchored version is not obtainable paired. Tooling constraint on the human arm: prospective label-based barcoding is impossible in a human pregnancy, so the only usable primitive is endogenous - mtDNA variants via mtscATAC-seq or MAESTER (PMID 35210612), or somatic epimutations (PMID 40399669) - and their clonal resolution depends on prior clonal expansion (PMID 40134031), which is precisely what is in dispute for a polyclonal blood NK pool.
nearest_occupant: Tatematsu BK & Sojka DK, Mucosal Immunology 2025, PMID 39708955, "Tissue-resident natural killer cells derived from conventional natural killer cells are regulated by progesterone in the uterus." What it did: parabiosed mice plus intravascular antibody labeling to separate truly tissue-resident from blood-borne cells, combined with ovariectomy at 3 weeks and hormone add-back (progesterone, medroxyprogesterone 17-acetate) and a progesterone-receptor antagonist. What it established: uterine trNK cells are derived from peripheral conventional NK cells, and that derivation is progesterone-dependent and progesterone-expandable. How it differs from T5, precisely, on four axes: 1. SPECIES/COMPARTMENT. Mouse uterus and estrous-cycle uterus, not human first-trimester decidua basalis/parietalis. T5's compartment B (CD9+CD49a+CD56superbright first-trimester dNK) has no mouse equivalent with matching markers, and the mouse work is largely non-pregnant/peri-implantation. 2. LIGAND. Progesterone as a systemic hormone, not glycodelin-A. GdA is the downstream progesterone-driven decidual glycoprotein in humans; mice have no GdA acting in the way the claim requires. So the mouse result establishes THAT the conversion route exists under progesterone, while leaving entirely open WHICH progesterone-induced decidual factor executes it. That "which factor" question is a mechanism question, not a clonal-structure question, so the residual unoccupied part of T5 is the part clonal barcoding cannot decide anyway. 3. TOOL CLASS. Parabiosis + intravascular staining is a compartment-origin/chimerism assay: it says the tissue pool is fed from the circulating pool. It is not the barcoding primitive (do these two cells share an ancestor and how recently). A barcode could in principle still add clone-level resolution (e.g., whether one blood clone seeds many dNK, or dNK are polyclonally seeded), but the yes/no origin answer is already in hand. 4. STARTING GATE. Mouse cNK is the DX5+/CD49b+ circulating pool, closest to human CD56dim; T5 nominates human CD16-CD56bright specifically. Note that the one true clonal-barcode result bearing on that gate, Wu et al. Sci Immunol 2018 PMID 30389798, found CD56+CD16- NK do NOT feed the mature CD16+ pool in macaque blood, i.e., the barcoding field's answer for the CD56bright-as-precursor premise in the periphery has already been NO in the one place it was tested. Two co-nearest occupants that matter as much: - Strunz et al., Sci Transl Med 2026, PMID 41811987: human UTx and HSCT with SNP/HLA-based single-cell donor-vs-recipient origin assignment; recipient cells replace donor immune cells in transplanted endometrium, and HSCT gives near-complete donor-derived endometrial reconstitution including tissue-resident lymphocytes. This is the human answer to "are uterine tissue-resident lymphocytes progeny of the circulating/BM pool" and it is YES. Differs from T5 by being non-pregnant endometrium (not GdA-high decidua), by not being NK-specific, and by using genetic origin rather than clonal barcodes. - Wu et al., Front Immunol 2022, PMID 36605190: lentiviral barcoded autologous HSPC transplant in rhesus, clonal comparison of blood vs tissue-resident T, B, myeloid and NK across liver, spleen, lung, GI, LN. This is the exact instrument T5 would need, already built and validated for NK. It has simply never been pointed at uterus/decidua, and the animals were not pregnant.
crossfield_occupancy: Yes, heavily occupied across all three fields, and in two of them the same structural question is considered settled. T CELL FIELD (uses TCR as a free endogenous barcode, so it has been ahead of NK on this question for a decade): - Poon et al., Nat Immunol 2023, PMID 36658238, "Tissue adaptation and clonal segregation of human memory T cells in barrier sites": paired blood + multiple tissues from the same organ donors, TCR clonotype sharing used to ask exactly "is the tissue compartment the progeny of the blood compartment." Answer: partial sharing with substantial clonal segregation, i.e., the tissue pool is not simply a converted blood pool. - PMID 38422982 (2024), "Dynamic establishment of recipient resident memory T cell repertoire after human intestinal transplantation": donor/recipient chimerism plus TCR repertoire tracking over time in human transplanted gut. This is the exact design that the human uterine field is now copying via UTx/HSCT (PMID 41811987), and it answers the recruitment-vs-residency origin question directly. - Snyder/Zuber-type solid-organ transplant TRM work generally: the "circulating precursor converts to tissue-resident phenotype" claim has been adjudicated with genetic origin markers, not phenotype, since the mid-2010s. Implication for T5: the T cell field's verdict is that the honest answer is usually "partially, with clonal segregation," not a clean yes/no. A dNK result is likely to land in the same ambiguous middle, which is exactly the zone where a lineage answer is least actionable. ILC FIELD: - ILC1/ILC2/ILC3 plasticity has been fate-mapped in mouse for years (Rorc-fate map, Bcl11b, T-bet driving ILC3-to-ILC1 conversion in gut/liver/inflamed mucosa; see review PMID 38563448 and the mechanistic literature cited inside PMID 41782473). - Critically, T-bet fate mapping has ALREADY been run on decidual NK specifically: PMID 41782473 (2026). Its conclusion is that dNK do NOT undergo lineage diversion despite losing T-bet, they adapt transcriptionally. That is the ILC field's tool answering the decidual version of the plasticity question already. - Flommersfeld et al., Immunity 2021, PMID 34437840: single-cell fate mapping/barcoding of mouse NK identified an ILC1-like lineage bridging innate and adaptive recognition, i.e., single-NK-cell clonal fate has been resolved in vivo. - Vo et al., Blood Adv 2024, PMID 38484189: human DNA-barcode clonal tracing separating NK from noncytotoxic ILC developmental routes in vitro. MYELOID FIELD: - Liu et al., Cell 2019, PMID 31491389, Ms4a3-Cre fate mapping: cleanly separated monocyte-derived from embryonically-seeded tissue macrophages and effectively closed the "does the circulating cell become the tissue cell" question for macrophages. This is the canonical demonstration that this structural question is answerable and, once answered with a proper lineage tool, stops being a research program. NK-INTERNAL CROSSFIELD: - The macaque barcoding program (PMIDs 24702997, 29141868, 30389798, 36605190) has already applied the exact primitive to NK ontogeny, NK subset interconversion, and blood-vs-tissue NK clonal relationships. Human adaptive NK clonality has been read out with natural somatic markers (Corat et al., Blood 2017, PMID 27903532, PIGA-mutant clones in PNH; Rueckert et al., PMID 36289449, clonal expansion and epigenetic inheritance of NK memory). Bottom line on borrowed occupancy: T5 borrows "differentiation/plasticity of a circulating cell into a tissue-adapted cell." Every field it borrows that from has already answered it with a lineage tool, and the reproductive-immunology field itself has now answered it twice (mouse parabiosis PMID 39708955; human transplant chimerism PMID 41811987). What remains unoccupied is only the GdA-as-the-driver part, which is a mechanism/causation question that the clonal barcoding primitive explicitly cannot decide.

why: FALSE — this is the reversible-state carve-out, and it fails on three independent grounds. (1) THE PREDICATE IS A STATE, NOT AN ANCESTRY RELATION. The claim is "IL-35 drives NK TOWARD a CD9+CD103+CD49a+ ILC1-like PHENOTYPE." Both operative terms are non-lineage: "toward ... phenotype" is directional state language, and "ILC1-like" is a functional/phenotypic predicate. The primitive (do two cells share an ancestor, how recently) returns nothing about whether a cell is ILC1-like. This is the rubric's "A becomes functionally B-like" case. (2) BOTH READINGS PRODUCE THE SAME CLONAL TOPOLOGY — the decisive point. The two live interpretations are (a) genuine differentiation of cNK into an ILC1-like cell, and (b) a reversible, cytokine-maintained surface program (three integrins/tetraspanin) layered on unchanged cNK. Under BOTH, barcodes straddle the CD49a-/CD49a+ boundary: clones appear in both marker fractions at intermediate timepoints and the whole day-0 repertoire is represented by day 8. There is no barcode topology that separates "converted" from "transiently up-regulated ITGA1/ITGAE/CD9," because no lineage branch is created in either case. Clonal structure is degenerate with respect to the question actually being asked. The 48 h washout non-reversal reported by the source does not rescue this — 48 h of marker persistence is not a heritable branch, and the cross-field literature says the program is generic and reversible over longer horizons (Fonseca ex-TRM, PMID 32066954; Zitti Immunity 2023, PMID 37269830, showing IL-15+TGF-b induces CD49a and a TRM program on CIRCULATING human CD8 T cells, RUNX2/RUNX3-dependent — i.e. the same integrin program is cross-lineage and therefore not lineage-diagnostic). (3) THE CAUSAL CLAUSE IS OUTSIDE THE PRIMITIVE. "IL-35 drives" is a perturbation-attribution claim. Lineage supplies no causal attribution; and the proximal cause in the source's own data is autocrine TGF-b (fully abrogated by anti-TGF-b1/2/3 and Galunisertib, reproduced by TGF-b alone), so the clause is one step upstream of the measured mechanism regardless of any clonal readout. WHAT IS DECIDABLE, AND WHY IT DOES NOT SAVE THE ROW: there is a narrow lineage-shaped residue the claim does not assert — "is the CD9+CD103+CD49a+ population the clonal progeny of marker-negative cNK, or the outgrowth of a pre-existing, clonally distinct subset?" That is a legitimate same/different-lineage question and is decidable in principle (mtDNA-variant tracking or lentiviral barcoding on day-0 blood NK, indexed on the marker triad). This is why T6 is a near-miss rather than a trivial FALSE. But it is not the claim, it fails B2 below, and it is gated on a marker definition the field itself calls unresolved: Wu et al. (PMID 36605190, PMC9808525), the only primate barcode study of blood-vs-tissue NK clonality, states outright that "definitive markers to distinguish NK from ILCs in tissues remain unresolved" and that they "are not able to exclude the presence of ILCs." A clonal answer inherits the gate it is asked to adjudicate; if "ILC1-like" is defined by the very markers in dispute, the barcode result is only as meaningful as the sort. (Decidability here does not depend on the Phase A dispute over the primary source's verification status — the claim's structure fails the primitive either way.)

Concretely, all three next moves are non-clonal: (a) REAGENT QC — assay PeproTech 200-37 single-chain IL-35 (HEK293, 406-aa IL12A-EBI3 fusion, used at 100 ng/mL) against vehicle on a Ba/F3-gp130-IL-12Rb1-IL-12Rb2 reporter with pSTAT1/pSTAT4 readout, i.e. the Aparicio-Siegmund assay (PMID 25259790), because if the recombinant is inactive or carries a TGF-b-inducing contaminant the clonal result is about a different molecule entirely. compartments_needed: Two distinct compartment sets, depending on which version of the claim is adjudicated. VERSION 1 — the in vitro claim as actually evidenced (population-frequency shift in culture): A. Day-0 human peripheral blood CD56+CD3- NK, prospectively gated CD9-CD103-CD49a- (the marker-negative starting compartment). B. Day-4 and day-8 CD9+CD103+CD49a+ cells from the IL-35 arm of the SAME well. B'. Day-4/day-8 marker-NEGATIVE cells from that same well (the within-well comparator that makes the straddle-vs-partition read possible; without it there is no boundary to test). C. The paired IL-2-alone well from the SAME donor. All four come from one buffy coat or leukapheresis from one healthy donor, split across wells. Same individual by construction. VERSION 2 — the in vivo claim the result is deployed to support (tumour NK are IL-35-converted ILC1-like cells): A. Autologous peripheral blood cNK from the patient. B. Tumour-infiltrating CD9+CD103+CD49a+ group-1 ILC from the resected lesion. C. Adjacent non-malignant tissue from the same organ (to separate tumour-driven from tissue-intrinsic residency). D. A compartment defined by prior IL-35 EXPOSURE — required for the "IL-35 drives" clause, and it does not exist as a sortable population. OPTIONAL PHYSIOLOGICAL COMPARATOR (if one wants the natural human CD9+CD49a+ compartment rather than tumour): decidual NK, for which CD9+CD49a+ is the canonical hallmark; or liver-resident CD49a+ NK.

VERSION 1: FULLY OBTAINABLE, PAIRED, FROM ONE HUMAN, WITH NO ANATOMICAL OR ETHICAL CONSTRAINT. crossfield_occupancy: HEAVILY OCCUPIED — G4 fires strongly. T6's structural question, stripped of IL-35, is: "are cells bearing tissue-residency markers the clonal progeny of circulating marker-negative cells of the same type, or a separate lineage?" That question has been asked and answered with lineage tools in all three neighbouring fields, and in two of them the answer is already known. T CELL FIELD — ANSWERED, and answered first, because T cells carry a free endogenous barcode (the TCR) that NK cells lack. The residency marker in question is literally the same molecule, CD103/ITGAE, induced by the same cytokine, TGF-β. Gaide O et al., "Common clonal origin of central and resident memory T cells following skin immunization," Nat Med 2015, PMID 25962122 — TCR-clonotype adjudication showing skin-resident and circulating memory compartments descend from common clones. Klicznik MM et al., "Human CD4+CD103+ cutaneous resident memory T cells are found in the circulation of healthy individuals," Sci Immunol 2019, PMID 31278120 — the CD103+ tissue-resident phenotype is clonally continuous with blood, i.e. CD103 positivity is a STATE, not a lineage boundary. (Both confirmed at PMID/title level, not read to methods.) This is the single most important cross-field result for T6: the field that borrowed T6 its marker and its cytokine already determined that the TGF-β/CD103 residency phenotype does not partition the clonal tree. Any lineage adjudication of T6 would be re-running, on NK cells, an experiment whose answer in the neighbouring lineage is on the books. ILC FIELD — ANSWERED for the adjacent conversion. Muraoka WT, ... Tumanov AV, "Campylobacter infection promotes IFNγ-dependent intestinal pathology via ILC3 to ILC1 conversion," Mucosal Immunol 2021, PMID 33214656 / PMC8084871 — RORγt-Cre × ROSA26-YFP cell-fate mapping (methods confirm the Rorc-Cre and ROSA26-YFP alleles) established that the pathogenic IFNγ+T-bet+ NK1.1- ILC1-profile population develops FROM RORγt+ progenitors, i.e. genuine ex-ILC3 conversion. Bielecki P et al., "Skin-resident innate lymphoid cells converge on a pathogenic effector state," Nature 2021, PMID 33536623 — fate-mapping of skin ILC convergence. And within group-1 ILC specifically, Flommersfeld 2021 (PMID 34437840) is the clonal answer described above: separate lineages, not conversion. So the ILC field has established BOTH outcomes are obtainable and has resolved them case by case with Cre-lox fate maps and single-cell barcoding — meaning T6's question is technically tractable but no longer structurally novel. MYELOID FIELD — ANSWERED, in the exact human compartment set T6 Version 2 needs. Liu V et al., Cancer Cell 2026, PMID 42242233: mtDNA clonal tracing across matched tumour/adjacent-normal/blood demonstrated that TME-resident myeloid subsets — macrophages and DC3 — are clonally linked to both circulating and tissue-infiltrating monocytes, while also resolving distinct DC-biased versus macrophage-biased clones enriched in tumour versus NILT respectively. That is precisely the "does a tissue-associated state map onto clonal structure?" question, run to completion in human cancer patients. Their quantitative myeloid result (mean 58.5% same-type fraction in myeloid clones vs 78-79% for T/B clones) is the template answer T6 would be reproducing on the NK/ILC1 axis. NET: the IL-35 wrapper is unoccupied and the NK/CD9-CD103-CD49a version is unoccupied, but the underlying structural question is occupied in T cells (answered: residency marker = state, clones shared), in ILC (answered both ways, case-dependent), and in myeloid (answered: tissue subsets clonally linked to circulating precursors, with clone-level state bias). The borrowed mechanism's occupancy lives in the T cell field it was borrowed from.
