why: DECIDABLE, but only in a specific reading, and two of the claim's three clauses have to be handled separately. The claim bundles (a) a PROVENANCE assertion — intratumoural NK descend from the NK pool that was in that organ, not from the circulating pool; (b) a TEMPORAL assertion — that ancestral pool was in the organ before the tumour; (c) a FUNCTIONAL rider — "functional" intratumoural NK. (a) is squarely the primitive's form ("the progeny of A are B" / "A and B are same-or-different lineage") and is DECIDABLE. The two competing hypotheses predict genuinely different clonal structures, not the same one: under X1, tumour NK coalesce recently with uninvolved-same-organ NK and only deeply (at the HSPC root) with blood NK; under the recruitment alternative (Torcellan 2024 PMID 38157853; Horowitz 2026 PMID 42090477) the reverse. The primitive's "how recently" term is what does the work — it separates "kin because both were seeded from the same marrow clone" from "kin because one locally divided into the other." This requires three compartments, not two; with only tumour+organ the answer is symmetric (organ->tumour, tumour->organ, blood->both are all consistent with the same sharing) and would fail. (c) is NOT lineage-decidable and must be discharged by construction, not by inference: "functional" has to become a sort gate on compartment B (GzmB+/degranulating/IFN-g+ intratumoural NK) so that lineage is asked about an already-functionally-defined bucket. Lineage must never be used to argue the cells are functional. (b) is decidable ONLY if the mark is applied before the tumour exists (photoconversion/inducible fate map/parabiosis at t0), which makes it a true lineage question — "do these tumour cells descend from the cells I marked in the organ." Read from a single post-tumour timepoint it is not a lineage property at all and must be imported as an assumption. WHY THIS IS NOT THE REVERSIBLE-STATE TRAP, and the condition under which it becomes one. Tissue residency IS a reversible/inducible state — Torcellan 2024 shows circulating NK acquire it, Horowitz 2026 shows TGF-beta is sufficient ex vivo, Blood 2025 (PMID 40857665) shows chronic activation installs a residency-like state via KLF2 loss. If X1 were phrased as "NK acquire residency inside tumours," both answers would be consistent with one clonal structure and it would be NOT DECIDABLE. But X1 is phrased as an origin claim: which pool did these cells come from. Provenance of a cell from compartment A versus compartment B is pedigree, not state. The state is the confound here, not the claim. CONDITION: this only holds if compartments A and B are defined SPATIALLY (cells physically in the uninvolved organ vs physically in the tumour, with i.v. anti-CD45 labelling to exclude vascular contamination). If compartment A is instead defined phenotypically as CD49a+CD103+CD69+ "trNK", the compartment is a reversible state, cells enter and leave it with no lineage event, and the claim collapses back into the undecidable form. The registry must fix the spatial definition or this row is not decidable. SECOND CONDITION, from the registry's own ontology. Because this registry treats ILC1 as distinct from NK (T4, P3), a positive result is only about X1 if the marked cells are NK-lineage — otherwise it is Dadi 2016 (PMID 26806130) again, whose resident population is Nfil3-independent and transcriptionally "distinct from conventional NK cells," and whose cNK showed HIGH non-host chimerism. Usefully, that fork is itself a lineage question the same primitive answers (do the tissue cells coalesce with blood cNK, or with an ILC-progenitor-derived clade — cf. Nixon 2022 PMID 35394814, "did not interconvert with NK cells"), so it can be settled inside the same experiment rather than assumed.
action_if_yes: YES = tumour NK coalesce recently with uninvolved-organ NK and only at HSPC depth with blood NK; the pre-tumour organ label is recovered inside the established tumour. VERY NEXT EXPERIMENT: convert the pre-tumour lineage label into a functional handle and selectively ablate ONLY the resident-derived pool, before tumour induction, in the autochthonous model. Concretely: pre-tumour photoconversion or inducible Ncr1/Hobit-driven marking of the uninvolved organ in an animal carrying an inducible DTR restricted to the marked cells; deplete the marked resident pool at t0; read tumour incidence and growth against (i) unlabelled controls and (ii) a recruitment-blocked arm (S1PR/chemokine-axis blockade) that leaves the resident pool intact. This is the experiment the field currently states it cannot do — "the current lack of experimental tools to block recruitment of circulating NK cells or to specifically target the newly identified resident cells currently precludes testing this possibility" — and a YES is exactly what licenses building the tool. WHY IT IS NOT VACUOUS: a YES makes the resident pool the causally load-bearing compartment and selects a specific therapeutic lever — preserve/expand the resident pool, i.e. the IL-15 axis chosen on residency grounds (Nixon 2022 PMID 35394814, with a filed MSKCC patent on targeting ILC1 IL-15 signalling; supported by Dadi's Il15-/- acceleration versus Nfil3-/- no-effect). It also re-reads the CD49a+ NK prognostic literature in HCC (PMID 31311791) as a genuine residency pedigree rather than a TME-exposure readout. Second, cheaper follow-on available immediately from the same clonal data: test at clone resolution whether the intratumoural clones are the same clones that were locally proliferating pre-tumour — i.e. put Dadi's EdU inference (local proliferation, not immigration) on a clonal footing.
action_if_no: NO = tumour NK coalesce with blood NK and are no more related to uninvolved-organ NK than the HSPC-root baseline; the pre-tumour organ label is absent or negligible inside the tumour. VERY NEXT EXPERIMENT: a different design on a different compartment — label the CIRCULATING pool at defined times relative to tumour onset (serial photoconversion of blood/spleen, or HSPC barcoding with staggered induction) and measure (i) entry timing and dwell time of intratumoural NK, and (ii) whether a SINGLE recruited clone gives rise to both CD49a+CD103+ "trNK-like" and conventional intratumoural progeny. Point (ii) is the decisive one and is not asked at all on the YES branch: it distinguishes in-situ diversification from one entrant versus separate entrants with pre-set fates, which is precisely the Flommersfeld 2021 (PMID 34437840) selection-versus-conversion fork that those authors named for tumours themselves. The macrophage field has already run this exact design with photoconversion (PMID 40523200: dwell-time-dependent divergence of monocyte-derived TAM fates), so the protocol is off the shelf. WHY IT IS NOT VACUOUS: a NO flips the therapeutic lever from preserve-the-resident-pool to promote-recruitment-then-impose-residency, which is the Horowitz ex-vivo TGF-beta ctrNK manufacturing route (PMID 42090477) — and a NO would establish that the manufactured product recapitulates a real in vivo route rather than a flask artefact, which is currently unknown. It also inverts the causal reading of the CD49a+ HCC prognostic signal (pedigree -> TME-exposure biomarker), and it demotes the IL-15/resident axis as a mis-chosen lever. Within this registry it hands the phenomenon to T1 (cNK -> trNK) with a specific, differently designed test rather than terminating inquiry.
compartments_needed: FIVE compartments, needed simultaneously and ideally from one individual. The first three are mandatory; C is the one most often omitted and its absence is fatal. A. NK resident in the UNINVOLVED SAME ORGAN — defined spatially (in the organ, i.v. anti-CD45-negative), not by CD49a/CD103/CD69, and critically resident there BEFORE the tumour existed. B. NK INSIDE THE ESTABLISHED TUMOUR, gated functionally at sort (GzmB+/degranulating/IFN-g+) so the "functional" clause is a sorting criterion rather than a lineage inference. C. CIRCULATING NK (blood, and spleen in mouse). MANDATORY DISCRIMINATOR — without it, shared clones between A and B cannot be separated from common marrow ancestry and neither answer is reachable. D. BONE MARROW / HSPC compartment, to set the deep-coalescence null: how related are any two NK from this individual by marrow output alone. Without D there is no baseline for "how recently" and the primitive's discriminating term is unusable. E. An ILC1 / ILC-progenitor-derived comparator from the same tissue, required by this registry's own ontology (T4, P3 treat ILC1 as distinct from NK). Without E a positive result may be an ILC1 result mislabelled as trNK — precisely the fork that made Dadi 2016 unusable for this row.
compartments_obtainable: PARTIAL. Obtainable in full from one mouse; NOT obtainable in full from any human, and the compartment that fails in humans (A with its pre-tumour timepoint) is the one carrying the claim's temporal clause. HUMAN. A+B+C paired from one person: YES, but AT SURGERY ONLY, and only in organs where tumour-free same-organ tissue is resected alongside the tumour. why: Three independent reasons, any one of which is sufficient. (1) THE TERMINAL NODE IS A FUNCTION, NOT A POPULATION. "Tumour NK -> pro-angiogenic phenotype" is the canonical "A becomes functionally B-like" form. The load-bearing content is VEGF secretion / angiogenesis promotion. Clonal barcoding reports shared ancestry and its recency and nothing else; it cannot report whether a cell secretes VEGF or remodels vessels. The functional half of the claim is outside the primitive's range entirely. (2) "DECIDUAL-LIKE" IS AN ANALOGY, NOT AN ANCESTRY ASSERTION, AND THE TWO NAMED COMPARTMENTS CANNOT BE CLONALLY COMPARED EVEN IN PRINCIPLE. dNK and tumour NK reside in different tissues and, in essentially every realisable case, different individuals. Clonal relatedness between cells from two different humans is not merely unmeasured, it is undefined: somatic mtDNA variants sit on individual-private germline haplotypes, and lentiviral barcodes are per-recipient. Asking "do these share a recent ancestor" across donors has no answer the primitive can return. The claim's headline comparison therefore poses no lineage question at all — Phase A's INF_MARKER grading is exactly right about the epistemic move being made (CD56bright CD16- VEGF+ resemblance), and marker resemblance is not an ancestry relation. (3) THE ONLY WELL-FORMED RESIDUAL QUESTION IS A REVERSIBLE-STATE QUESTION. Reformulated intra-patient — "are intratumoural CD56bright CD16- VEGF+ NK the progeny of the same recent ancestors as that patient's circulating CD56dim NK, or a clonally distinct compartment?" — this has the decidable same/different-lineage shape. But CD56bright/CD16-/VEGF+ is an inducible, non-heritable cell state, so both answers are consistent with the same clonal structure: - SHARED CLONES is consistent with (a) in-situ conversion of infiltrating cNK, and equally with (b) recruitment of a pre-existing CD56bright subset that of course shares ancestry with CD56dim, since all NK in one person converge on a common HSC/NK-progenitor pool and the "how recently" cut-off is set by the analyst, not by the biology. - NO SHARED CLONES is consistent with (a) a genuinely separate tissue-resident/ILC-like origin, and equally with (b) sparse clone capture — the expected null when clone sizes are small (see Wang et al., Genome Biol 2025, PMID 40134031: clonal expansion dictates the efficacy of mtDNA lineage tracing). Because the state is reversible and not transmitted through the clonal record, the barcode partition is invariant to which hypothesis is true. Empirically this is already visible: PMID 42242233 (Cancer Cell 2026) recovered BOTH patterns for NK in the same study — expanded NK clones shared with blood/non-involved tissue in some patients, and tumour-restricted NK clones absent from matched blood in another — without that bit resolving any state-transition question.
action_if_yes: YES = intratumoural pro-angiogenic NK share recent clones with matched peripheral blood NK (blood-derived infiltrators). Very next experiment: an induction/perturbation assay. Take autologous peripheral blood NK, expose to tumour-conditioned medium and to candidate TME drivers individually (TGF-beta, hypoxia/HIF, adenosine, PGE2, IL-15 withdrawal), read out acquisition of CD56bright CD16- VEGF+ and angiogenic output (HUVEC tube formation / aortic ring). Then block the winning driver in vivo and ask whether intratumoural VEGF+ NK frequency and microvessel density fall. Note this is precisely the experiment already performed without any lineage input: PMID 32655841 (renal cell tumours convert NK to a pro-angiogenic phenotype) and PMID 30597092 (glycodelin-A converts blood CD16- CD56bright NK to a dNK-like phenotype) both ran the conversion assay directly.
action_if_no: NO = no shared clones between intratumoural pro-angiogenic NK and matched blood NK. Very next experiment: first, a methods response, not a biological one — sequence more cells, more timepoints, and deeper mtDNA coverage to exclude the sampling-failure explanation, because a negative is the expected artefact under sparse clone capture. Only after that survives do you go looking for the alternative source (adjacent normal tissue NK, bone marrow NK progenitors, tissue-resident ILC1) — and having found a candidate source, the next step is again an induction/perturbation assay: expose that source population to TME signals and ask what drives the VEGF+ CD56bright state, then block it. The biologically informative move in this branch is therefore the same assay as the YES branch, reached one step later and after a round of "sample deeper".
compartments_needed: For the claim AS WRITTEN, two compartments simultaneously: A = decidual NK (CD56bright CD16-) from decidua basalis/parietalis — first-trimester decidua at elective termination, or term decidua/placental bed at delivery. B = tumour-infiltrating NK from a solid tumour — surgical resection or core biopsy. For the reformulated intra-patient version, up to five: B = tumour-infiltrating NK (surgery/biopsy) C = matched peripheral blood NK (venepuncture) D = adjacent non-involved tissue NK (same surgical specimen) E = bone marrow NK progenitors (separate aspirate) and, to anchor the "decidual-like" comparison at all, A again as an unpaired cross-donor reference.
compartments_obtainable: NO for the pair the claim actually names (A + B); YES for the reformulated intra-patient set (B + C + D). A + B paired from one human: not obtainable in practice. Decidua is available ONLY during pregnancy — first-trimester termination or term delivery. Tumour is available only at surgery or biopsy. Pairing them requires a pregnant cancer patient undergoing tumour resection and decidual sampling in the same window; such cases exist as isolated reports but cannot be assembled into a cohort, and the co-occurrence is itself confounded (pregnancy-associated malignancy is not typical tumour biology). More fundamentally, the fallback of comparing A from donor 1 against B from patient 2 is not a lineage comparison at all. Shared ancestry between cells from different individuals is undefined for both mtDNA variants (individual-private germline haplotype background) and lentiviral barcodes (per-recipient). Unpaired dNK-vs-tumour-NK sampling can only ever regenerate the marker resemblance Phase A already logged as INF_MARKER — it cannot upgrade it to a lineage statement. B + C + D paired from one human: routinely obtainable, and already done. This is exactly the NSCLC design in PMID 42242233 (tumour resection + non-involved lung + PBMC from the same patient). Adding E requires a separate marrow aspirate — obtainable but an extra invasive procedure, rarely consented alongside tumour surgery. Archived/frozen material is now tractable via cryo-mtscATAC-seq (PMID 41000852), which relaxes the fresh-tissue constraint but does nothing about the A+B pairing problem.

why: TRUE, but only narrowly, and only for a weaker proposition than the claim asserts. WHAT IS DECIDABLE. The claim's testable core reduces to the rubric's second decidable form, "A and B are the same/different lineage": do intratumoural NK3_GZMK and NK3_ENTPD1 cells in one NSCLC tumour draw from the same clones, or from clonally disjoint pools? That is a pure clonal-structure question and the primitive answers it directly. It is also live rather than academic, because the paper contradicts itself on exactly this point: the published version's cross-modality section concludes the taNK branches "represent distinct lineages that converge transcriptionally, while retaining their ancestral chromatin marks," while the abstract asserts "an inflammation-driven transition from early GZMK+ NK cells toward an ENTPD1+ effector state." Clonal sharing versus disjointness adjudicates between those two sentences. WHY THE REVERSIBLE-STATE CARVE-OUT DOES NOT FULLY VOID IT. The carve-out applies to a reversible state *within one lineage*. Here the leading alternative is not a state-flicker model but a two-population model with a genuinely different clonal signature: NK3_GZMK as recently immigrated circulating CD56bright NK (GZMK marks CD56bright, Bratke 2005 PMID 16106370), NK3_ENTPD1 as a pre-existing locally imprinted CD49a+CD103+NKG2C+ lung trNK pool that expands in tumour (Brownlie 2021 PMID 33836578). One-lineage versus two-lineage is not a within-lineage state question, so the arrow is refutable. WHY IT IS ONLY HALF DECIDABLE — the part that matters for B2. The primitive returns shared ancestry and its recency; it never returns the STATE of the ancestral node. So it cannot order the arrow. Shared clonotypes are produced identically by (a) GZMK+ -> ENTPD1+, (b) ENTPD1+ -> GZMK+, (c) a common precursor branching into both, and (d) one clone reversibly flickering through an inducible endpoint — and (d) is not hypothetical here, since ENTPD1/CD39 is an activation-inducible ectoenzyme that the authors themselves induce on healthy-donor blood NK in six days with IL-15+TGF-beta, and the ISG-high program (IFIT3, IFI44, ISG15) is an hours-scale reversible interferon response layered on any NK cell. Direction cannot be recovered from tip states without an assumed root, which is precisely the defect Phase A found in the original analysis (Monocle3 start "defined as the terminal branch within the NK3_GZMK population"; destiny root "selected from the NK3_GZMK cluster"). NET: the claim is REFUTABLE by clonal structure but not CONFIRMABLE by it. Recorded TRUE because a disjoint-clone result would kill the arrow outright; the asymmetry is carried into B2, where it is fatal.
action_if_yes: IF YES — NK3_GZMK and NK3_ENTPD1 nuclei from the same resection share mtDNA clonotypes above a matched-donor permutation null. nearest_occupant: Liu VV, Sandor K, Yan PK, ... Lareau CA, Satpathy AT. "Clonal lineage tracing of innate immune cells in human cancer." Cancer Cell 2026;44(7):1509-1521.e4. PMID 42242233; preprint PMID 40777278 / PMC12330704 (full text archived at /home/user/aaa/refs/X4_PMC12330704.txt). WHAT THEY DID: mtscATAC-seq (joint scATAC + mtDNA genotyping) with a new clone-caller, Mitotrek, that "prioritizes fidelity of clonal assignments over detection sensitivity." 218,715 cells. NSCLC cohort: patient-matched lung tumour + non-involved lung tissue (NILT) + PBMC from 5 patients. Ovarian cohort: primary tumour + matched PBMC, 5 patients (3 with blood). This is X4's compartments 1, 2, 3 and 4, paired from one human, in the same disease, with the exact primitive X4 proposes. It is the closest a paper can get without being the paper. HOW IT DIFFERS — four ways, each disqualifying: (a) NK SUBSET RESOLUTION IS ABSENT. Verbatim: "4 NK cell/ILC clusters (NCR1)" in the joint object and "3 NK/ILC clusters (NCR1)" in the tumour-only reclustering; annotation markers for the T/NK compartment were "CD3D (broad T), CD8A (CD8+ T), CD4 (CD4+ T), GNLY, NCR1 (NK/ILC), FOXP3 (Treg)." GZMK, ENTPD1, ITGAE and ITGA1 never appear as NK annotation axes. NK3_GZMK and NK3_ENTPD1 were never separated, so the A->B clonal test was never posed, let alone answered. (b) THE NSCLC ARM HAD NO NK CELLS TO TRACE. Verbatim: "depletion of NK cells in the tumor relative to NILT" and "While NK cells were rarely detected in most tumors ...". X4's entire primary comparison is intratumoural-A versus intratumoural-B in lung; that cell yield did not exist in this dataset. (c) THE ONE NK-RICH TUMOUR WAS OVARIAN, AND THE QUESTION ASKED WAS EXPANSION, NOT ANCESTRY. Verbatim: "one ovarian tumor (SU-O-005) exhibited substantial NK infiltration ... These NK cells lacked chromatin accessibility at CD3D and CD8A loci but showed accessibility at NCR1 and GNLY, confirming their NK identity ... Notably, expanded NK clones were absent from matched peripheral blood, indicating a tumor-restricted NK response." That is a compartment-restriction result (tumour vs blood), not a state-to-state ancestry result. Separately, in NSCLC: "we observed expanded NK cell clones in NILT and peripheral blood," and among blood-enriched clones "2 by NK cells from a single donor (SU-L-005)." (d) THEIR GENERAL NK STATEMENT ACTIVELY UNDERCUTS X4'S RESOLVABILITY. Verbatim: "innate immune cells, including monocytes, macrophages, DCs, and NK cells, consistently exhibited high levels of clone sharing, suggesting that they originated from recent hematopoietic output without substantial clonal bottlenecks prior to tissue infiltration." Promiscuous clone sharing across innate states is the regime in which "A and B share ancestors" is uninformative — it is what you see whether or not A converts to B. This converges with Rückert's null in conventional NK (PMID 36289449). SECOND NEAREST, ON THE PRECURSOR ARCHITECTURE ITSELF: Wu C, Espinoza DA, ... Bryceson YT, Dunbar CE. "Clonal expansion and compartmentalized maintenance of rhesus macaque NK cell subsets." Sci Immunol 2018;3(29):eaat9781. PMID 30389798 / PMC7393805. Barcoded autologous HSPC transplant, >4 years. Asked X4's exact structural question one level up — is the CD56bright-like subset the clonal source of the mature effector subset? — and answered NO: oligoclonal CD56-CD16+ NK "remained long-term clonally uncoupled from other hematopoietic lineages, including CD56+CD16- NK cells," KIR-segregated, maintained by "peripheral compartmentalized self-renewal," with "linear NK cell production from multipotent hematopoietic progenitors or less mature CD56+CD16- cells ... negligible during homeostasis and moderate proliferative stress." Differs from X4: macaque, blood, non-tumour, CD16/CD56 rather than GZMK/ENTPD1, and homeostasis rather than an inflamed TME. THIRD, ON THE TISSUE-VS-BLOOD ARM: Wu C, Liang JA, ... Dunbar CE. PMID 36605190 / PMC9808525. Same barcoded model extended to liver, spleen, lung and GI versus blood. Found tissue-restricted NK clone sets (lung-specific, GI-specific; liver/spleen-shared) and expanded blood DN clones feeding tissue NK — "but absent in CD56+16- TR NK across all tissues analyzed." This is X4's compartment-3/4 question (local product vs pre-existing tissue-resident pool vs recent immigrant) answered with real barcodes — but in macaque, without tumour, and without the GZMK/ENTPD1 axis.
crossfield_occupancy: X4 invokes local differentiation/plasticity plus tissue residency. Every adjacent field has already run this exact structural question through a lineage tool, and the answers are heterogeneous enough that X4 cannot borrow a presumption from any of them. MYELOID — FULLY OCCUPIED, SAME DATASET, POSITIVE ANSWER. Liu et al. 2026 (PMID 42242233) is the myeloid version of X4 and it worked: TME-resident macrophages and DC3 are clonally related to circulating and tissue-infiltrating monocytes, with DC-biased and macrophage-biased clones whose blood precursors already carry distinct epigenetic profiles — "intratumoral myeloid differentiation fate may be peripherally programmed before TME infiltration." Note what this does to X4: the same authors, same tumours, same assay found that the intratumoural state's origin was NOT local conversion but a peripherally pre-programmed bias. That is precisely X4's Brownlie-2021 alternative, confirmed in the neighbouring lineage of the same tissue. MOUSE NK — OCCUPIED, AND IT FLIPPED A PSEUDOTIME STORY. Flommersfeld S et al. "Fate mapping of single NK cells identifies a type 1 innate lymphoid-like lineage that bridges innate and adaptive recognition of viral infection." Immunity 2021;54:2288-2304. PMID 34437840 / PMC8528403 (archived). Retrogenic colour barcoding of SINGLE Ly49H+ NK cells transferred into Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- hosts, MCMV, clones read at d8. Verbatim: "progeny derived from single Ly49H+ NK cells showed limited diversification and instead adopted one of two distinct fates"; the two fates "originated from two distinct NK cell lineages present already during the steady state and stably maintained throughout infection" (CD62L+ cNK vs CD62L-CD160+ ILC1-like, splenic-resident). A phenotypic continuum that reads as one lineage differentiating was resolved by clonal fate mapping into two pre-existing lineages. This is the canonical demonstration in the NK field that the lineage primitive can invert a trajectory claim — and it is exactly X4's competing hypothesis. MOUSE NK->TISSUE-RESIDENT CONVERSION IN TUMOURS — CLAIMED, NEVER BARCODED. Gao Y et al. "Tumor immunoevasion by the conversion of effector NK cells into type 1 innate lymphoid cells." Nat Immunol 2017;18:1004-1015. PMID 28759001; companion Cortez VS et al. "SMAD4 impedes the conversion of NK cells into ILC1-like cells." Nat Immunol 2017;18:995-1003. PMID 28759002. TGF-beta-dependent conversion of CD49a-CD49b+Eomes+ NK into CD49a+ intILC1/ILC1 in the mouse TME, established with "global transcriptomic and flow-cytometry analyses and genetically engineered mouse models" plus adoptive transfer — population-level fate, no clonal barcode. So the mouse analogue of X4 (conventional NK converting locally into a CD49a+ tissue-resident-like intratumoural state) is asserted in the literature but has never itself been clonally adjudicated. Human in-vitro versions exist too (TGF-beta+IL-15, PMID 32332109; IL-35, PMID 40610398) and are equally non-clonal. T CELL — HEAVILY OCCUPIED VIA TCR AS THE LINEAGE TOOL, AND THE ANSWER IS OFTEN "NOT LOCAL CONVERSION." Yost KE et al., Nat Med 2019;25:1251-1259, PMID 31359002 — clonal replacement: the post-treatment intratumoural exhausted pool was largely NEW clones from outside, not locally converted residents. Wu TD et al., Nature 2020;579:274-278, PMID 32103181 — peripheral clonal expansion predicts tumour infiltration. Pai JA et al., Cancer Cell 2023;41:776-790.e7, PMID 37001526 — TCR lineage tracing of clonal progenitors and long-term persistence during ICB. Krishna C et al., Cancer Cell 2021;39:662-677.e6, PMID 33861994 — multiregional TCR linking tissue-resident T cells to tumour topology. The T-cell field's verdict is that recruitment/replacement is real and frequently dominant over local conversion — which is exactly why X4 must carry compartments 3 and 4, and why a YES on X4 would not be a foregone conclusion. ILC — OCCUPIED WITH FATE MAPPING. ILC3->ILC1 conversion adjudicated by fate mapping (PMID 33214656, Campylobacter); Bielecki P et al., Nature 2021;592:128-132, PMID 33536623, "Skin-resident innate lymphoid cells converge on a pathogenic effector state" — convergence of resident ILC subsets onto one effector state, the same shape as X4's convergence onto NK3_ENTPD1. Also PMID 38484189 (Blood Adv 2024), clonal + single-cell analysis separating human NK from noncytotoxic ILCs. NET: the question shape is answered everywhere around X4, with lineage tools, and the answers split — myeloid says peripherally pre-programmed, mouse NK says two pre-existing lineages, T cells say frequently replacement — so no field supplies a default X4 can inherit. The NK-specific slot for this exact pair of intratumoural human states is genuinely empty.

why: NOT DECIDABLE. Two independent defeaters, either sufficient on its own, plus a third minor one. (1) THERE IS NO OPERAND B. The primitive answers "do A and B share an ancestor, and how recently." That presupposes A and B can each be POINTED AT — sorted at the bench by a rule fixed in advance and independent of lineage. "Exhausted NK" is not such a rule. The label was assigned by explicit analogy — Gill 2012 (PMID 22544698): "We have termed this phenomenon 'NK-cell exhaustion' by analogy with similar findings in CD8+ T cell biology" — and has never been given operational content in NK cells. PD-1 is near-absent/disputed on NK (in Gill it was negative and consigned to "data not shown"); TIGIT/TIM-3/LAG-3 are non-specific; there is no NK chromatin or DNA-methylation signature of the state (no equivalent of Sen 2016 PMID 27789799 / Pauken 2016 PMID 27789795); and the T cell field's defining enforcer TOX (Khan 2019 PMID 31207603) is a DEVELOPMENTAL requirement in NK cells (Aliahmad 2010 PMID 20818394), so it is unavailable as a definition and is in fact inverted. Under the field's own consensus criteria for the borrowed term (Blank 2019 PMID 31570879) the first anchor — chronic antigen through a clonotypic receptor — is undefined by construction in NK, which have no clonotypic receptor. With no gate for B there is no lineage question, only a naming dispute. There is also a circularity hazard: defining B post hoc as "the cells lineage places downstream of functional NK" uses lineage to define the state and then lineage to prove the transition. (2) THE REVERSIBLE-STATE TRAP, AND IT SURVIVES STIPULATION. Suppose we generously stipulate B := intratumoural NK that fail to degranulate / produce IFN-g on restimulation. NK effector capacity is a demonstrated BIDIRECTIONAL, DIVISION-INDEPENDENT rheostat. Elliott 2010 (PMID 20819924) transferred hyporesponsive b2m-/- NK into non-irradiated WT hosts; they reached host-WT IFN-g levels by ~day 4, stably, receptor-restricted (Ly49C+ but not Ly49C-), with NO CFSE dilution. Baseline heterogeneity is likewise established, not hypothetical: a large hyporesponsive fraction exists in every healthy animal by education status (Anfossi 2006 PMID 16901727; Joncker 2009 PMID 19342631), and hyporesponsive NK can preferentially dominate an in vivo response (Orr 2010 PMID 20190757). Consequently both answers produce the SAME clonal structure: - Barcodes SHARED between the functional and hypofunctional buckets is predicted by conversion (A->B), by the reverse (B->A, Elliott), by continuous bidirectional traffic, and trivially by one clone being sampled at two rheostat settings on the same day. - Barcodes NOT SHARED is predicted by selection/outgrowth of a pre-existing hyporesponsive clone (Mavilio 2005 PMID 15699323 titled the human phenotype as a dysfunctional subset "expanded" in viremic HIV) AND equally by conversion in which the converted cell's functional siblings died or exited the sampled compartment. Neither observation licenses a direction. The state is not clonally heritable, so it is not a lineage property, and the primitive is structurally blind to it. (3) RESIDUAL FUNCTIONAL PREDICATE. "Exhausted" means hierarchical functional loss. "A becomes functionally B-like" is out of scope for a primitive that measures only shared ancestry. NARROW READING THAT WOULD BE DECIDABLE — recorded for completeness, and it is NOT this claim: "is the hypofunctional intratumoural NK pool clonally DISTINCT from, or interleaved with, the functional intratumoural NK pool" is of the same/different-lineage form, and the how-recently term does real work there. But that is R2/T4's question rather than X5's, and it still fails B2 below, so promoting X5 by rewriting it does not rescue it.
action_if_yes: YES = barcodes/mtDNA clones are SHARED across the two buckets; hypofunctional intratumoural NK coalesce recently with functional NK in the same tumour rather than only at the HSPC root. Very next experiment: sort the hypofunctional bucket and ask whether the state is FIXED or a setting — transfer it into a tumour-free host (or withdraw the cytokine/ligand stimulus), re-read function at 4 and 10 days against a within-recipient comparator, and in parallel run ATAC-seq and DNA methylation on both buckets to ask whether a distinct, stable epigenetic state exists at all. Note what this is: a reversibility test plus a state-definition assay. Neither uses the lineage primitive. And the reversibility half already has a published answer in the opposite direction (Elliott 2010, PMID 20819924), so the YES branch mostly re-opens a question that has been answered against the claim by a better-controlled design than Gill's.
action_if_no: NO = the hypofunctional cells sit in clones that do not contain functional cells; the two buckets are clonally separate at recent depth. Very next experiment: sort the hypofunctional bucket and ask what it actually IS — education/licensing status, adaptive PLZF-low NKG2C+ identity (Schlums 2015 PMID 25786176, which carries the same surface reading, the opposite label, and SUPERIOR ADCC), or the CD56-CD16+ expanded subset (Mavilio 2005 PMID 15699323) — then test whether that subset's state is fixed or revertible by transfer/stimulus withdrawal, with ATAC and methylation on both buckets. That is the identical experiment as the YES branch, reached from the other side. And the conclusion half is close to vacuous on its own: "the label was wrong, these are a pre-existing selected subset" is a re-description the literature has had available since 2005 and has not adopted, so producing it again changes no downstream decision.
compartments_needed: Four things must be in hand at once, from one individual: A (candidate precursor) — functional NK, contemporaneous. Practical instantiations: (i) matched peripheral blood NK; (ii) NK from uninvolved same-organ tissue adjacent to the tumour; (iii) intratumoural NK passing a LIVE functional gate (surface CD107a degranulation, or IFN-g secretion-capture) after short restimulation. B (candidate product) — "exhausted" intratumoural NK. NO AGREED GATE EXISTS; this is the reason the row fails B1. Stipulated proxies would be the functional-assay-negative fraction from the same restimulation, or contested surface proxies (NKG2D-lo, TIGIT+, CD56-CD16+, PD-1+), none of which is validated as a state definition. C (outgroup/root) — matched blood or bone-marrow NK, MANDATORY, not optional. Without a third compartment the "how recently" term cannot be exercised, and A/B sharing is uninterpretable because all NK share an HSPC ancestor by construction. D (mouse instantiation of the same set) — donor splenic NK at t0, plus tumour, spleen and blood at t1 in the Gill-type transfer model.
compartments_obtainable: TISSUE ACCESS IS THE EASY PART, and this is the only dimension on which X5 scores well. Paired tumour + adjacent uninvolved tissue + peripheral blood from ONE HUMAN is routine at surgical resection (lung, colorectal, renal, hepatocellular, breast). Tumour and adjacent-normal are SURGERY-ONLY — not obtainable from a living donor by any other route — while blood and marrow pair freely. Nothing here requires post-mortem tissue, nothing requires pregnancy, nothing is restricted to mouse. The mouse transfer model additionally gives all four compartments trivially from one animal. BUT THE BINDING CONSTRAINT IS NOT ACCESS — IT IS THAT A AND B ARE NOT TWO COEXISTING PLACES. The claim's A is "the same cell BEFORE it became exhausted," which is a time point, not a compartment, and is destroyed by the act of measuring it. Clonal barcoding substitutes SIBLINGS for the ancestral state; that substitution is licensed only if the state is clonally heritable over the sampling window. Elliott 2010 (PMID 20819924) — full reversion in ~4 days with no cell division — says it is not. So the compartment pair that would actually decide X5 is unobtainable IN PRINCIPLE, in every species, for reasons that have nothing to do with consent, surgery, or tissue banking; while the compartment pair that IS readily obtainable decides a different and weaker question.
nearest_occupant: Two occupants, in different senses. Neither is the claim. (1) NEAREST CLONAL OCCUPANT — Liu et al., Cancer Cell 2026, PMID 42242233. Has the method (mtscATAC-seq), has all four compartments paired from one human (tumour + NILT + blood), and does report an intratumoural NK clonal result. HOW IT DIFFERS, precisely: it partitions NK by TISSUE, not by STATE. Its NK finding is "expanded intratumoural NK clones were absent from matched peripheral blood" in a single ovarian tumour — i.e. it answers A(i)-vs-B compartment sharing and returns a NEGATIVE, whereas claim X5 asks about A-vs-B within the tumour across a functional/exhausted boundary. It never gated NK on function, never applied an exhaustion definition, and ran a fixed-cell assay that structurally excludes the live CD107a/IFN-g gate that claim X5's compartment A(iii) and B require. n=1 informative tumour. So the specific adjudication is open, and this paper is the demonstration that the reagent exists and the yield does not. (2) NEAREST OCCUPANT OF THE UNDERLYING BIOLOGY, non-clonal — Dean I, Lee CYC, ... Clatworthy MR, Withers DR. "Rapid functional impairment of natural killer cells following tumor entry limits anti-tumor immunity." Nat Commun 2024;15:683. PMID 38267402. Kaede photo-labelling of tumours plus longitudinal transcriptomics: circulating NK recruited into the tumour rapidly lose effector function and adopt a distinct CD49a+ tissue-residency-like dysfunctional state. This is a population-level fate map with a timestamp, NOT a clonal method — it cannot say whether two cells share an ancestor — but it already answers the directional question X5 is a proxy for ("functional NK entering the tumour become the dysfunctional intratumoural cells") at population resolution, in mouse, decisively. Any clonal version of X5 would be re-answering with a costlier primitive a question this paper has closed. (3) LOAD-BEARING FOR WHY X5 IS NOT A LINEAGE QUESTION AT ALL — Pouxvielh K et al. "Tumor-induced natural killer cell dysfunction is a rapid and reversible process uncoupled from the expression of immune checkpoints." Sci Adv 2024;10:eadn0164. PMID 39196934. The state is REVERSIBLE and uncoupled from the very surface proxies (checkpoints) that claim X5's compartment B would have to be gated on. A reversible state leaves no clonal signature: a clone straddling both states and a clone confined to one state are both consistent with an interconverting state, so the clonal read-out does not discriminate. This corroborates the B1 failure independently of the occupancy question. Also checked and NOT the claim: Vo DN et al. Blood Adv 2024;8:2933-2951 (PMID 38484189), DNA-barcode tracing separating human NK from non-cytotoxic ILC along development — clonal, NK, but developmental origin, in vitro, no tumour. Gill S et al. Blood 2012;119:5758-5768 (PMID 22544698), the Gill-type transfer model named in compartment D — adoptive transfer, no barcodes, no clonal resolution.
crossfield_occupancy: HEAVILY OCCUPIED. The structural question "are the dysfunctional/exhausted cells in a tumour the clonal descendants of the functional ones, or a separate lineage?" has been asked and answered with clonal tools in the T cell field, and with the identical mtDNA tool in the myeloid field. NK is the last compartment to be asked, and the answer elsewhere has repeatedly been that the clonal read-out under-determines the state question. T CELL — answered, multiple times, with the native clonal barcode (TCR): - Yost KE et al. Nat Med 2019;25:1251-1259 (PMID 31359002). Paired scRNA+TCR-seq, basal cell carcinoma, pre/post PD-1. The exhausted CD8 TIL pool that expands after PD-1 blockade consists of NOVEL clonotypes not previously detected in the tumour — "clonal replacement". This is exactly the X5 structure (does the exhausted compartment descend from the resident functional one, or arrive separately?) answered with a clonal primitive, with a NEGATIVE answer for the intuitive model. - Pai JA et al. Cancer Cell 2023;41:776-790.e7 (PMID 37001526). "Lineage tracing reveals clonal progenitors and long-term persistence of tumor-specific T cells during immune checkpoint blockade" — establishes clonal linkage between TCF7+SELL+ progenitor-exhausted cells in the draining lymph node and their exhausted counterparts in the tumour. The precursor-to-exhausted-product lineage relation is settled. - Wu TD et al. Nature 2020;579:274-280 (PMID 32103181) — peripheral clonal expansion predicts tumour infiltration; the blood-to-tumour clonal bridge, i.e. exactly the compartment A(i)-to-B question X5 poses. - Luo Y et al. Cancer Immunol Res 2026;14:32-45 (PMID 41081433) — single-cell clonal lineage tracing of neoantigen-specific CD8 fate decisions; the same question at single-clone resolution in mouse. - Yamaguchi A et al. Oncoimmunology 2026 (PMID 41787604) — Pdcd1-CreERT2 genetic fate mapping. Notably, PD-1-fate-mapped NK cells in tumours LOST PD-1 and REGAINED FUNCTION, i.e. a genetic fate map has already shown the NK "exhausted" state to be exited, reinforcing that this is a reversible state and not a lineage endpoint. MYELOID — answered with the SAME mtDNA tool, in the SAME paper, in the SAME patients: Liu et al. (PMID 42242233) resolved that TME macrophages and DC3 are clonally related to circulating and tissue-infiltrating monocytes, and identified DC-biased vs macrophage-biased clones with peripherally programmed fate bias. The myeloid arm of that paper is what an NK arm would have looked like had NK yields permitted and had a state definition existed. The authors could run the NK version and did not. ILC — partially occupied and methodologically instructive: Vo DN et al. Blood Adv 2024 (PMID 38484189) used DNA-barcode lineage output to place NK relative to non-cytotoxic ILC, showing S3b-NK and S4-NK are closely related while ILC3 is distant. So the ILC field has used clonal tools for lineage-vs-state discrimination among innate lymphocytes; the reason it has not done so for "exhaustion" is that ILC plasticity is likewise treated as a reversible state. Net: the mechanism X5 borrows (exhaustion) originates in the T cell field, and its occupancy lives there. The T cell field needed an ANTIGEN-SPECIFIC clonal barcode plus a validated, epigenetically anchored state definition (TOX/TCF7) to make the question decidable. Claim X5 has neither — no agreed exhaustion gate for NK, and a native barcode (mtDNA) that is state-agnostic.
